docs.text: Logic Events ¶ Logic events are frame-bound actions stored inside an animation's events array in logic.json . They are useful when you want deterministic animation behaviour without writing Lua. Event Shape ¶ Every event includes a $type field: { "$type": "Sor2NewEra.Gameplay.SoundEvent, Sor2NewEra", "frame": 4, "packName": "My Pack", "soundName": "punch-heavy" } Most events also include frame . Events that operate across a frame window use afterFrame and beforeFrame instead. Editor Name to JSON Type ¶ The Character Editor shows events under short display names, while the saved JSON uses class names. They do not always match in an obvious way — Set Anim is JumpToAnimationEvent , and Set Value is SetCustomValueEvent . Use this table to move between the editor and hand-edited JSON. Editor name JSON $type Set Velocity VelocityEvent Set Acceleration AccelerationEvent Input -> Velocity InputVelocityEvent Input -> Acceleration InputAccelerationEvent Set Pos Offset PositionOffsetEvent Stop StopEvent AccX(0) -> Stop StopOnHorizontalStop Set Anim JumpToAnimationEvent Input Button -> Set Anim JumpToAnimationOnInputButton Input Combo -> Set Anim JumpToAnimationOnInputCombo Hit -> Set Anim JumpToAnimationOnHit Land -> Set Anim JumpToAnimationOnLanding Land -> Set Frame JumpToFrameOnLanding AccX(0) -> Set Frame JumpToFrameOnHorizontalStop Spawn Enemy SpawnEnemyEvent Spawn Item SpawnItemEvent Grab GrabEvent Flip FlipEvent Destroy DestroyEvent Set Invincibility InvincibilityEvent Add Health HealthEvent Set Value SetCustomValueEvent Play Sound SoundEvent Play Music MusicEvent Event List ¶ Event Main fields Use AccelerationEvent frame , acceleration , useAxisFlags , affectX , affectY , affectZ Set acceleration. Axis flags enable each component input and let zero values affect one component without resetting the others. VelocityEvent frame , velocity , useAxisFlags , affectX , affectY , affectZ Set velocity. Axis flags enable each component input and let zero values affect one component without resetting the others. InputAccelerationEvent strength Apply input-driven acceleration on every frame of the animation. InputVelocityEvent afterFrame , beforeFrame , strength Apply input-driven velocity during a frame window. StopEvent frame Stop movement. StopOnHorizontalStop none Stop when horizontal motion stops. FlipEvent frame Flip facing direction. PositionOffsetEvent frame , offset fields Move the object by an offset. InvincibilityEvent frame , invincible Enable or disable invincibility. HealthEvent frame , health Add health. Use a negative value for a cost or damage. DestroyEvent frame Destroy or deactivate the object. GrabEvent frame Attempt grab behaviour. JumpToAnimationEvent frame , animationId , animationFrame Change animation at a fixed frame. JumpToAnimationOnHit afterFrame , beforeFrame , animationId Change animation if hit during a window. JumpToAnimationOnInputButton afterFrame , beforeFrame , animationId Change animation on button input. JumpToAnimationOnInputCombo afterFrame , beforeFrame , input , animationId , ignoreDuringSlowMotion Change animation on input sequence. The optional slow-motion guard skips activation without clearing input history. JumpToAnimationOnLanding initialFrame , animationId , animationFrame Change animation when landing. JumpToFrameOnLanding initialFrame , jumpFrame Jump to a frame when landing. JumpToFrameOnHorizontalStop initialFrame , jumpFrame Jump to a frame when horizontal motion stops. SoundEvent frame , packName , soundName or soundNames Play a sound. MusicEvent frame , packName , musicName Schedule or play music. SpawnEnemyEvent frame , packName , entityName , animationId , mode Spawn an enemy. SpawnItemEvent frame , packName , entityName , animationId , mode , positionOffset , velocity Spawn an item or projectile. SetCustomValueEvent frame , valueId , value Set one custom value slot. Spawn Item Event ¶ SpawnItemEvent can also include projectile metadata: { "$type": "Sor2NewEra.Gameplay.SpawnItemEvent, Sor2NewEra", "frame": 12, "packName": "My Pack", "entityName": "Fireball", "animationId": 0, "mode": -1, "lifetime": 60, "positionOffset": { "x": 12, "y": 0 }, "velocity": { "x": 520, "y": 0 }, "isProjectile": true, "damage": 8, "hitPause": 4, "hitSoundName": "fireball-hit", "hitSoundPack": "My Pack", "hitSoundChannel": 1 } Events And Animation Behaviour ¶ If an animation defines events, the animation does not run the default referenced Classic move controller for that animation. This protects custom event-based animations from original mode side effects. Movement, branching, spawning, and other default behaviour must then be provided by events, Lua, or the local default physics step. If you want the original behaviour to run, keep the animation's events array empty and use referenceBehaviour . When To Use Lua Instead ¶ Use Lua when event data would need branching: if target distance is less than a threshold if the player pressed a custom sequence if health is below a value if a target exists and is on the same line See Lua Scripting . Full field reference ¶ For the complete field list of every event, the axis and window semantics, and worked examples, see Entity Files .

docs.text: Mod Config ¶ config.json defines a pack's identity, dependencies, game settings, and optional pack-level scripts. For the complete field-level specification, including every session setting and the full difficulty tables, see Pack Config . Minimal Shape ¶ { "id": "3f6c2a9e-8b1d-4c57-9e2f-7a0d5b4c1e88", "isChronicle": true, "description": "My Streets of Rage 2 New Era mod.", "dependencies": ["Classic"], "dependenciesChecksums": [""], "settings": { "hasWideScreen": true, "hasImprovements": true, "bufferGlitchFixMode": 2, "scoreForLives": [20000, 50000, 150000], "difficultySettings": [] } } Editor-created packs usually contain a much larger settings object. Keep it unless you know which game-session behavior you are changing. Top-Level Fields ¶ Field Type Description id string Stable unique identifier: a random UUID created once with the mod and never changed. The engine identifies the pack by it, so a rename keeps every reference. Mods without one are identified by name. See Mod identity . isChronicle bool Marks the pack as a Chronicle-style content pack. expandHudSpacing bool In widescreen, reserve a 32px lane beside the timer for custom HUD art. Defaults to false . If the campaign or any active character pack enables it, all player HUDs use the expanded layout. description string Description shown by menus or pack listings. dependencies string[] Pack names this pack depends on. Classic reskins should include Classic . dependenciesChecksums string[] Optional checksum list matching dependencies . Empty strings are accepted in editable packs. dependenciesIds string[] Optional id of each dependency, matching dependencies ; null for one without an id. settings object Game-session settings. preEntityUpdateScripts ScriptData[] Scripts run before entity updates. postEntityUpdateScripts ScriptData[] Scripts run after entity updates. Common settings Fields ¶ Field Description hasWideScreen Enables widescreen presentation support. hasImprovements Enables New Era improvements for the session. bufferGlitchFixMode Input buffer fix mode. 0 no fix, 1 all but ground upper, 2 all. scoreForLives Score thresholds for extra lives. difficultySettings Difficulty definitions. See Difficulty Settings . scrollSpeedMultiplier Fraction object applied to scroll speed. useSmoothControls Enables smoother control behavior. emulateClassicLag Enables classic lag emulation. allowedCharacters Optional list of allowed character pack/type hashes. minimumPlayers Minimum player count. maximumPlayers Maximum player count. -1 means no explicit maximum. Multiplier Fields ¶ Multipliers are stored as fractions: { "numerator": 3, "denominator": 2 } This example means 1.5x . Pack-Level Scripts ¶ Pack-level scripts use the same ScriptData shape as animation scripts: { "preEntityUpdateScripts": [ { "packName": "My Pack", "scriptName": "Global entities pre-update" } ] } Use these sparingly. Animation scripts are easier to reason about because they only run when an entity reaches that animation. Dependency Guidance ¶ Classic reskins should include Classic in dependencies . Packs that replace Classic art, audio, palettes, or entities usually target Classic folder paths, so the dependency tells the runtime that those original assets are expected.
docs.title: Mod Config Reference

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ This page collects common modding failures and the first places to check. Pack Does Not Appear ¶ Check: pack folder is under Editor/<Pack Name> while editing config.json is valid JSON folder name does not start with a dot dependencies in config.json are available thumbnail.png is valid if the menu tries to show it Classic Reskin Does Not Apply ¶ Check: dependencies includes Classic reskin level files are under Level Replacements/Classic entity replacements are under Entity Replacements/Classic audio maps are under Audio Replacements/Classic playable palettes are under Palettes/Classic/<Playable Character> Image Missing In Level Editor Or Game ¶ Check: imageName exactly matches a file in Levels/Art extension is included in imageName the image is not in Level Replacements/Classic the layer has the image in staticImages , titleScreenImages , or animation frames the JSON scene has at least one layer Title Screen Still Uses Original ¶ Check: file is Level Replacements/Classic/title.json the pack is loaded as a Classic reskin title JSON has a scenes array visible art is in staticImages or titleScreenImages old Levels/title.json was migrated or removed if the editor created a skin copy Script Does Nothing ¶ Check: script file is in Scripts/ scriptName omits .lua packName matches the pack folder name the animation reaches the scripted frame the script returns its update function, and that function returns true context object is not nil Use print() temporarily and check the Unity log or in-game error display. Script Throws Nil Errors ¶ Guard context-specific objects at the start of the update function: local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end Do the same for attacker , victim , nearest opponents, and objects returned from ID lookup. Music Does Not Play ¶ Check: music file is in Musics JSON uses the base filename without extension musicPackName or replacement packName matches the pack name replacement map is Audio Replacements/Classic/music-replacements.json loop metadata JSON is valid if present Sound Does Not Play ¶ Check: sound file is in Sounds JSON uses the base filename without extension replacement map is Audio Replacements/Classic/sound-replacements.json event frame is reached sound channel is appropriate Palette Does Not Appear ¶ Check: the workflow is for playable characters only path is Palettes/Classic/<Playable Character>/palette <n>.png PNG dimensions and color order match the expected palette guide the pack was reloaded after adding files Entity Replacement Loads Wrong Behavior ¶ Check: entityType is correct referencePackName and referenceEntityName point to the intended original entity referenceBehaviour.objectMode uses a valid value from Behaviour Modes animations with events intentionally skip referenced Classic behaviour spawned entity names and pack names match exactly

docs.text: Audio Files ¶ Audio is split into what your pack owns and what it replaces in another pack. Sounds/ owned sound effects and voices Musics/ owned music tracks Musics/<track>.json loop points for one track Audio Replacements/ <Target Pack>/ music-replacements.json redirect that pack's music to yours sound-replacements.json redirect that pack's sounds to yours Owned audio ¶ Drop audio files into Sounds/ or Musics/ . Supported formats are .wav , .mp3 , and .ogg . Everything references audio by base file name, without the extension. Sounds/heavy-hit.wav -> "heavy-hit" Musics/stage-1.ogg -> "stage-1" That name is what goes in logic.json sounds groups, a SoundEvent 's soundName , a hitbox's soundName , an art file's musicName , and a Lua play_sound call: game.this_character.play_sound("My Pack", "heavy-hit", 1) Anything in these folders that is not a .json file is treated as an audio asset, so keep stray files out. Sound names must be unique within a folder regardless of extension. punch.wav and punch.ogg are the same name "punch" , and which one wins is not defined. Music loop points ¶ A music track loops from the start by default. To loop a section, add a JSON file beside the audio with the same base name: Musics/Fighting In The Streets.ogg Musics/Fighting In The Streets.json { "loopStartTimeInSeconds": "8.132", "loopEndTimeInSeconds": "32.865" } Field Meaning loopStartTimeInSeconds Where the loop restarts from. loopEndTimeInSeconds Where the loop jumps back from. 0 or omitted loops at the end of the clip. loopTimeInSeconds Legacy name for the loop start, read only when loopStartTimeInSeconds is absent. Prefer the explicit pair. The Audio Editor writes these values as JSON strings , as shown. Plain numbers work too. Either way they are parsed with invariant culture, so the decimal separator is a dot regardless of the player's locale — a loop point of 12.5 behaves the same on a machine that formats numbers with a comma. Times are in seconds and are converted to sample positions against the clip's own sample rate, so they stay correct whatever the file's encoding. Replacing another pack's audio ¶ To use your audio in place of another pack's — nearly always Classic — add a replacement map under Audio Replacements/<Target Pack>/ . The target pack's own files are untouched; the redirect lives entirely in your pack. Both files are plain objects keyed by the target pack's audio identifier. music-replacements.json ¶ Keys are Classic music identifiers such as M00 , M03 , M06 . { "M00": { "packName": "My Pack", "musicName": "Stage 1 Remix" }, "M03": { "packName": "My Pack", "musicName": "Fighting In The Streets V2" } } sound-replacements.json ¶ Keys are Classic sound slot numbers, written as strings. { "0": { "packName": "My Pack", "soundName": "hit-1" }, "13": { "packName": "My Pack", "soundName": "power-blast" } } In both files, packName is the pack providing the replacement, normally your own, and the name resolves inside that pack's Musics/ or Sounds/ folder. You only list what you are replacing. Anything absent from the map keeps the target pack's original audio, so a partial replacement map is perfectly normal. An empty map, or one that fails to parse, is skipped entirely — no replacements are registered and no error is raised. If a replacement seems to do nothing, check the file parses and that the folder name matches the target pack exactly. Which mechanism to use ¶ You want Use A new sound for your own character's punch Owned audio in Sounds/ , referenced from logic.json . Your own music on your own level Owned audio in Musics/ , referenced from the level's - art.json . Every Classic punch to sound different sound-replacements.json . Classic Stage 1's music replaced music-replacements.json . A sound at one exact animation frame A SoundEvent in logic.json . The music to change mid-animation A MusicEvent in logic.json . docs.text: Audio is split into what your pack owns and what it replaces in another pack. Sounds/ owned sound effects and voices Musics/ owned music tracks Musics/<track>.json loop points for one track Audio Replacements/ <Target Pack>/ music-replacements.json redirect that pack's music to yours sound-replacements.json redirect that pack's sounds to yours
docs.title: Audio Files

docs.text: Drop audio files into Sounds/ or Musics/ . Supported formats are .wav , .mp3 , and .ogg . Everything references audio by base file name, without the extension. Sounds/heavy-hit.wav -> "heavy-hit" Musics/stage-1.ogg -> "stage-1" That name is what goes in logic.json sounds groups, a SoundEvent 's soundName , a hitbox's soundName , an art file's musicName , and a Lua play_sound call: game.this_character.play_sound("My Pack", "heavy-hit", 1) Anything in these folders that is not a .json file is treated as an audio asset, so keep stray files out. Sound names must be unique within a folder regardless of extension. punch.wav and punch.ogg are the same name "punch" , and which one wins is not defined.
docs.title: Owned audio

docs.text: A music track loops from the start by default. To loop a section, add a JSON file beside the audio with the same base name: Musics/Fighting In The Streets.ogg Musics/Fighting In The Streets.json { "loopStartTimeInSeconds": "8.132", "loopEndTimeInSeconds": "32.865" } Field Meaning loopStartTimeInSeconds Where the loop restarts from. loopEndTimeInSeconds Where the loop jumps back from. 0 or omitted loops at the end of the clip. loopTimeInSeconds Legacy name for the loop start, read only when loopStartTimeInSeconds is absent. Prefer the explicit pair. The Audio Editor writes these values as JSON strings , as shown. Plain numbers work too. Either way they are parsed with invariant culture, so the decimal separator is a dot regardless of the player's locale — a loop point of 12.5 behaves the same on a machine that formats numbers with a comma. Times are in seconds and are converted to sample positions against the clip's own sample rate, so they stay correct whatever the file's encoding.
docs.title: Music loop points

docs.text: To use your audio in place of another pack's — nearly always Classic — add a replacement map under Audio Replacements/<Target Pack>/ . The target pack's own files are untouched; the redirect lives entirely in your pack. Both files are plain objects keyed by the target pack's audio identifier.
docs.title: Replacing another pack's audio

docs.text: Keys are Classic music identifiers such as M00 , M03 , M06 . { "M00": { "packName": "My Pack", "musicName": "Stage 1 Remix" }, "M03": { "packName": "My Pack", "musicName": "Fighting In The Streets V2" } }
docs.title: music-replacements.json

docs.text: Keys are Classic sound slot numbers, written as strings. { "0": { "packName": "My Pack", "soundName": "hit-1" }, "13": { "packName": "My Pack", "soundName": "power-blast" } } In both files, packName is the pack providing the replacement, normally your own, and the name resolves inside that pack's Musics/ or Sounds/ folder. You only list what you are replacing. Anything absent from the map keeps the target pack's original audio, so a partial replacement map is perfectly normal. An empty map, or one that fails to parse, is skipped entirely — no replacements are registered and no error is raised. If a replacement seems to do nothing, check the file parses and that the folder name matches the target pack exactly.

docs.text: Pack Config ¶ config.json sits at the root of a mod folder and declares what the pack is, what it needs, and what rules it plays by. { "id": "3f6c2a9e-8b1d-4c57-9e2f-7a0d5b4c1e88", "isChronicle": true, "description": "My Streets of Rage 2 New Era mod.", "dependencies": ["Classic"], "dependenciesChecksums": [""], "settings": { "hasWideScreen": true, "hasImprovements": true, "bufferGlitchFixMode": 2, "scoreForLives": [20000, 50000, 150000], "difficultySettings": [] } } Every field is optional. An omitted field takes its type default. Top level ¶ Field Type Meaning id string The mod's stable unique identifier: a random UUID, created once with the mod and never changed. The engine identifies the pack by it, so renaming the mod keeps everything that refers to it. See Mod identity . isChronicle bool Marks the pack as a full Chronicle: a standalone campaign that appears as its own game, rather than a skin layered over another pack. Set during export when applicable. expandHudSpacing bool In widescreen, reserve a 32px lane beside the timer for custom HUD art. Defaults to false. If the campaign or any active character pack enables it, all player HUDs use the expanded layout. hudLayout object Optional normal and widescreen profiles configuring player columns, timer offsets, and lives counters in 8px tiles. See below. description string Text shown in mod listings. dependencies string array Names of packs this pack needs at load time. A Classic reskin must list "Classic" . dependenciesChecksums string array Checksum of each dependency, positionally matched to dependencies . Editable source packs have no checksum, so empty strings are normal; the exporter fills them in. dependenciesIds string array The id of each dependency, positionally matched to dependencies ; null for a dependency without one. Optional. When present, the dependency is found by its id, so it survives being renamed. The editor writes it when it saves the pack. preEntityUpdateScripts ScriptData array Lua scripts run once per frame before any entity updates. postEntityUpdateScripts ScriptData array Lua scripts run once per frame after all entity updates. settings object Session rules. The rest of this page. Mod identity ¶ A pack whose config.json has an id is identified by that id. A pack without one is identified by its name (its folder or file name), as before, and keeps working unchanged. Create it once, never change it. The id is a random UUID (version 4), such as 3f6c2a9e-8b1d-4c57-9e2f-7a0d5b4c1e88 . It is not derived from the name or anything else. The editor creates one for every new mod. Changing an id makes the mod a different mod: replays, saves, netplay and other mods' references to the old id stop finding it. Copying a mod folder copies its id. Give the copy a new id (or remove the field). When two loaded mods declare the same id, the second one is identified by its name and an error is logged. Built-in packs ( Classic , 30th Anniversary , Ninpo Kage Bunshin ) are always identified by name; an id on them is ignored. References by name keep working. Everywhere a pack is referenced by name — dependencies , a packName in entity, level or script data, an audio replacement or palette folder, additionalCharacters , a Lua argument — the name resolves to the pack's id. Any of them may also be written as the pack's id instead, which survives a rename of that pack. Folder names ( Palettes/<pack> , Audio Replacements/<pack> , Entity Replacements/Classic ) stay names. Recorded hashes. Fields that store a pack as a number, such as settings.allowedCharacters[].packHash , hold the hash of the id when the pack has one. Data recorded before a pack declared an id — old replays, saves, preferences, packHash values — holds the hash of its name and is translated to the id automatically. Netplay compares mods by id when they have one, so players may know the same mod under different names. HUD layout ¶ hudLayout contains independent normal and widescreen profiles. The campaign's profile takes precedence; otherwise the first existing player (in slot order) whose character pack supplies that profile selects it for the whole session. Profiles are not merged. A missing profile keeps the built-in layout, including expandHudSpacing if enabled. Set "hidden": true (beside the profiles) on the campaign to turn the built-in HUD off entirely: names, health bars, scores, lives, the clock (including TIME OVER) and the continue/game-over prompts. Characters' hudScript drawings still show, so the pack can draw its own HUD; they receive score and lives . Each profile accepts: Field Meaning leftPlayerX , rightPlayerX Absolute X tile coordinates of the left and right player HUD origins. Omitted/null values retain the built-in columns. Row placement and automatic slot relocation still apply. timerOffsetX , timerOffsetY Offsets from the built-in clock position, in tiles; default 0. Move both its frame and digits. lives Optional single-row lives counter layout. Omitted/null keeps the built-in large counter. lives accepts leftX , rightX , and y , relative to the player HUD origin (default 0), plus width (2 or 3 tiles, default 3). It displays total lives, clamped to 0–99, with an icon when space permits. Viewer-driven inactive counters remain hidden. Drawing and clearing use the same configured bounds, including when a player HUD moves to another slot. For example, a pack can move player columns outward and place its own art in the resulting space: { "hudLayout": { "widescreen": { "leftPlayerX": -4, "rightPlayerX": 27, "timerOffsetX": -1, "lives": { "leftX": 18, "rightX": -6, "y": 2, "width": 3 } }, "normal": { "lives": { "leftX": 15, "rightX": 15, "y": 3, "width": 2 } } } } Custom meter sprites and their relative positions belong to the entity's hudScript ; the engine interprets only these layout coordinates. A ScriptData is { "packName": "...", "scriptName": "..." } , resolving to Scripts/<scriptName>.lua inside packName . The .lua extension is optional. Every pack you reference anywhere — a sprite reference, a logic reference, a spawned entity, a replacement target, a borrowed sound — should appear in dependencies . A reference to a pack that is not loaded is not a load error; it fails later, silently, as a missing sprite or sound. Session settings ¶ settings is a GameSessionData . It is what makes a Chronicle play differently from Classic. Core rules ¶ Field Type Default Meaning hasWideScreen bool false Allow the wider-than-original playfield. hasImprovements bool false Enable the New Era quality-of-life changes over original ROM behaviour. Turning this off is what "Classic rules" means. bufferGlitchFixMode int 0 How far to go fixing the original sprite buffer glitch: 0 NoFix, 1 AllButGroundUpper, 2 All. emulateClassicLag bool false Reproduce the original hardware slowdown. useSmoothControls bool true Use modern smoothed input handling rather than the original stepped one. useCoupleEnemiesAdvanceCheck bool true Keep the original rule that the camera only advances once few enough enemies remain. initialPlayerHealth int max Starting health for players. scoreForLives int array none Score thresholds granting an extra life, ascending. Player count ¶ Field Type Default Meaning minimumPlayers int 1 Fewest players this pack supports. maximumPlayers int -1 Most players. -1 means the engine maximum. Optional mechanics ¶ Field Type Default Meaning hasEnemiesHittingEachOther bool false Enemy attacks damage other enemies. hasFriendlyDamage bool false Players can damage each other. Without it, players also cannot grab each other, and a thrown body never hits a player. thrownCharactersSparePlayers bool false With hasFriendlyDamage on, a character thrown by a player does not hit or knock down other players; players can still hit and grab each other. No effect without hasFriendlyDamage . keepDirectionOnHit bool false Do not force the victim to turn towards the attacker when hit. hasNinpoKageBunshin bool false Enable the ninja shadow-clone mechanic. hasKillerEnemies bool false Killer enemies: attack frames without a hitbox play for one update, and an attack that hits a player stuns and restarts instead of knocking down, so it chains. See Killer Mode . hasExplodingEnemies bool false Enemies explode on death. hasInstantSpawns bool false Skip spawn introduction sequences. hasInfiniteContinuesOverrider bool false Force infinite continues regardless of difficulty. Global multipliers ¶ These override the corresponding per-difficulty multipliers for the whole pack. Field Applies to enemiesHealthMultiplierOverrider Enemy health. enemiesDamageMultiplierOverrider Damage enemies deal. enemiesVelocityMultiplierOverrider Enemy movement speed. playersDamageMultiplierOverrider Damage players deal. scrollSpeedMultiplier Level scroll speed. A multiplier is a rational number, not a float: "enemiesHealthMultiplier": { "numerator": 3, "denominator": 2 } The game uses integer maths so that replays and netplay stay deterministic across machines. denominator must not be zero. Randomisation ¶ Field Type Default Meaning enemiesRandomizerMode int 0 Enemy randomiser mode. 0 disables randomisation. randomValue int 0 Seed used by the randomiser modes. enemiesMultiplier int 1 Multiplies how many enemies each wave spawns. Borrowing from other packs ¶ Field Type Meaning additionalCharacters string array Names of other packs whose playable characters are offered alongside this pack's own. additionalMechanics string array Names of other packs whose gameplay mechanics are layered onto this pack. Packs listed here should also be in the top-level dependencies . Restricting character select ¶ allowedCharacters limits character select to a specific list. An empty list means no restriction. "allowedCharacters": [ { "packHash": -346761093, "entityType": 1531339648 } ] Unlike everywhere else in these formats, this identifies characters by hash, not name : packHash is the hash of the pack's id when it has one (the lowercase, hyphenated UUID string), otherwise of the pack name, and entityType is the hash of the entity folder name. See the name hash for how to compute them. -346761093 is "Classic" . Difficulty settings ¶ difficultySettings is an ordered list. Index 0 is the easiest, and the in-game difficulty selection indexes into it. Per difficulty ( DifficultySetting ): Field Type Meaning name string Label on the difficulty screen. enemiesDifficulty int Difficulty level passed to enemy AI, and the value a loadcue's minimumDifficulty is compared against. maxInitialLives int Highest number of starting lives selectable. initialCredits int Continues granted at the start of a run. hasInfiniteContinues bool Never run out of continues. hasInstantEnemiesPulling bool Enemies close distance immediately instead of easing in. settingsPerNumPlayers array One entry per player count. settingsPerNumPlayers index n-1 applies to an n player game. Provide as many entries as maximumPlayers allows; the engine reads the entry matching the current player count. Per player count ( DifficultySettingPerNumberOfPlayers ): Field Type Meaning maxNumEnemies int Most enemies allowed on screen at once. enemiesHealthMultiplier Multiplier Enemy health. bossesHealthMultiplier Multiplier Boss health, separately from regular enemies. enemiesDamageMultiplier Multiplier Damage enemies deal. enemiesVelocityMultiplier Multiplier Enemy movement speed. playersDamageMultiplier Multiplier Damage players deal. enemiesOnScreenActivationMultiplier Multiplier Scales the on-screen enemy count that wave triggers compare against. timeActivationMultiplier Multiplier Scales wave timer thresholds. useNextSpawnsDifficulty bool Draw spawns from the next difficulty's loadcue set instead of this one's. { "name": "Very Easy", "maxInitialLives": 9, "initialCredits": 3, "settingsPerNumPlayers": [ { "maxNumEnemies": 5, "enemiesHealthMultiplier": { "numerator": 1, "denominator": 2 }, "bossesHealthMultiplier": { "numerator": 1, "denominator": 2 }, "enemiesDamageMultiplier": { "numerator": 1, "denominator": 1 }, "enemiesVelocityMultiplier": { "numerator": 1, "denominator": 1 }, "playersDamageMultiplier": { "numerator": 1, "denominator": 1 }, "enemiesOnScreenActivationMultiplier": { "numerator": 1, "denominator": 1 }, "timeActivationMultiplier": { "numerator": 1, "denominator": 1 } } ] } An editor-created pack ships a large, fully populated difficultySettings . Keep it unless you know which behaviour you are changing: an empty or short list narrows how many difficulties players can pick. docs.text: Entity Files ¶ An entity is a playable character, an enemy, an item, a container, or a piece of scenery. Everything about it lives in one folder: Entities/<Entity Name>/ own content Entity Replacements/Classic/<Entity Name>/ replacement for a Classic entity Both use exactly the same file set. The folder name is the entity name used by every entityName reference. File Required Purpose spriteSettings.json yes How many sprite frames the entity has, and where each one's pivot sits. animations.json yes Which frame is shown for how long, per animation. logic.json yes Gameplay behaviour: stats, boxes, events, scripts. dependencies.json no Declared references to other packs' assets. <i>.png as needed Own sprite frames, zero-based. portrait.png , preview.png no Character select art. Palettes/palette <n>.png no Palette guides for this entity. See Palette Files . Three ideas govern all of it: the sprite index model , the reference fallback model , and the parallel animation arrays . Get these right and the rest is data entry. The sprite index model ¶ Everything that names a sprite uses an effective index , and effective indices are not PNG numbers. An entity may borrow another entity's sprite frames by setting referenceEntityPackName and referenceEntityName in spriteSettings.json . When it does, the combined frame list is: index 0 .. R-1 the reference entity's frames, in its own order index R .. R+N-1 this entity's own frames, where own frame k is the file k.png R is the reference entity's total frame count. N is the length of this entity's pivots array. Without a reference, R is 0 and effective index k is simply k.png . This matters in three places: animations.json frames[].imageId is an effective index. spriteSettings.json iconIndex is an effective index. Changing the sprite reference changes R , which shifts every own frame's effective index. The Character Editor remaps imageId values when you change the reference; a hand edit must do the same. pivots defines the frame count, not the files. If pivots has 12 entries, the entity has own frames 0.png through 11.png . A 12.png sitting in the folder is invisible. A missing 7.png with a pivot at index 7 is a frame that draws nothing. The reference fallback model ¶ logic.json can set referencePackName and referenceEntityName to inherit behaviour from another entity, usually a Classic one. This is how "an Axel that plays like Axel but hits harder" is authored. The fallback rule is blunt and worth memorising: On an entity with a logic reference, every numeric field left at 0 , and every array left null , falls through to the referenced entity. So on a referencing entity you cannot say "this character's walk speed is zero". Writing "walkSpeed": 0 and omitting walkSpeed mean the same thing: use the reference's value. Fields that behave this way are marked falls through in the table below. sprite references and logic references are independent. An entity can borrow Classic Axel's art while inheriting Classic Blaze's logic, or borrow art with no logic reference at all. There is a second, per-animation reference: animationsLogic[i].referenceBehaviour , which borrows one Classic move controller for one animation. It is subject to an override rule described under Animation logic . spriteSettings.json ¶ Root object: SpriteSettingsData . Field Type Meaning scale float Uniform draw scale for own frames. 0 is treated as 1 . shadowAlwaysOn bool Draw the ground shadow even in states that normally hide it. useSourceAnimations bool Visual skins only: draw the original gameplay entity's animation sequence using this skin's frame providers. All source frame indices, including playable variants' appended frames, must exist in the skin. Gameplay logic stays unchanged. Defaults to false. pivots array of {x, y} floats One pivot per own frame, in pixels from the image's bottom-left corner: x from the left edge, y up from the bottom edge. Array length is the own frame count. iconIndex int Effective sprite index used as the HUD icon. -1 for none. referenceEntityPackName string Pack owning the entity whose frames are borrowed. referenceEntityName string Entity whose frames are borrowed. { "scale": 1.0, "shadowAlwaysOn": false, "iconIndex": 4, "pivots": [ { "x": 22.0, "y": 1.0 }, { "x": 22.0, "y": 1.0 } ] } A pivot is the point of the image that sits on the character's position — for a standing character, the point between the feet. Because y counts up from the bottom edge, a standing frame whose feet touch the bottom row has a pivot y of about 1 . animations.json ¶ Root object: AnimationsSetData , a single animations array. The array index is the animation id. For entities based on Classic behaviour, index i corresponds to the Classic AnimationId value i * 2 ; the full slot table is in Enums and Identifiers . Entries may be null to leave a slot empty. Never reorder the array. Per animation ( AnimationData ): Field Type Meaning name string Editor label. Cosmetic; the runtime addresses animations by index. frames array Ordered frames. referenceTotalFrames int Total frame count of the same animation on the reference entity, used by the editor to keep a reskin aligned with original timing. 0 when there is no reference. Per frame ( AnimationFrameData ): Field Type Meaning duration int Game frames this image is held. The game runs at 60 fps. imageId int Effective sprite index. Negative draws nothing. weapon object or null Optional weapon overlay. Weapon overlay ( AnimationFrameWeaponData ): Field Type Meaning direction int WeaponAngle : 0 Up, 1 UpLeft, 2 Left, 3 DownLeft, 4 Down, 5 DownRight, 6 Right, 7 UpRight. showBehind bool Draw behind the character rather than in front. position {x, y} int Offset from the character pivot, in pixels. { "animations": [ { "name": "Standing", "frames": [ { "duration": 8, "imageId": 0 }, { "duration": 8, "imageId": 1 }, { "duration": 10, "imageId": 2 } ] }, null, { "name": "Jump", "frames": [{ "duration": 4, "imageId": 12 }] } ] } The animation's length is the sum of its frame durations. That total is the timeline every frame number in logic.json is measured against. An event at "frame": 26 fires 26 game frames into the animation, which may be partway through the fourth image, not on the 26th image. logic.json ¶ Root object: LogicData . Identity and references ¶ Field Type Meaning entityType int 0 Player, 1 BasicEnemy, 2 Enemy, 3 PickUpItem, 4 Container, 5 Scenery, 6 Other. The Character Editor only offers 0-3. BasicEnemy marks a common street enemy the difficulty system may multiply; Enemy marks a boss-class entity. referencePackName string Pack to inherit logic from. referenceEntityName string Entity to inherit logic from. Movement ¶ Field Type Falls through Meaning walkSpeed int yes Walking speed. runSpeed int yes Running speed. jumpForce int yes Upward jump impulse. Falls through to the reference, then to the Classic per-character table. jumpDelayFrames int yes Crouch frames before leaving the ground. Combat ¶ Field Type Falls through Meaning globalBodyBox BoundingBox no Default hurt volume, used on every animation that does not define its own bodyBoxes . canUseWeapons bool no Whether the entity can pick up and use weapons. comboRepetitions int yes Times the standing attack chain repeats before the finisher. grabComboRepetitions int yes Times the grab attack repeats before the grab finisher. chargeDelay int no Frames a button must be held before a charged move is available. noChargeFlash bool no Players only: true turns off the white flash shown when holding attack completes the charge. The charge and the charged attack still work. Default false keeps the flash. grabRange int yes Horizontal reach of a grab attempt, in pixels. frontGrabOffset int yes Distance the victim snaps to when grabbed from the front. backGrabOffset int yes Distance the victim snaps to when grabbed from behind. heldFrontGrabOffset int no Distance this entity is held at when grabbed from the front, whoever grabs it (pixels; 0 = the grabber's frontGrabOffset ). heldBackGrabOffset int no Same, when grabbed from behind (0 = the grabber's backGrabOffset ). knockedDownQuakeEffect float yes Screen shake when this entity hits the ground knocked down. thrownQuakeEffect float yes Screen shake when this entity lands from a throw. BoundingBox is { "halfWidth": int, "height": int, "depth": int } . The volume spans -halfWidth..+halfWidth horizontally, 0..height upwards from the feet, and ±depth on the depth axis. Canonical globalCombatBounds and animation bodyBoxes[].combatBounds use enabled , xMin , xMax , heightMin , heightMax , depthMin , and depthMax . An optional regions array supplies disjoint hurt rectangles in the same entity-local coordinates. The outer rectangle still provides world and grab dimensions; attack contact must intersect one enabled region. Omit regions for one solid rectangle, or use an empty array for no hurt contact. Regions mirror with facing and scale independently of sprite rendering. The Character Editor preserves these regions when saving the outer rectangle. On an item that hits as a projectile, its body regions are also its striking rectangles: a hit needs one of them to meet the target (thrown bodies keep the outer rectangle). Projectile behaviour ¶ Applies when this entity is thrown or spawned as a projectile. Field Type Falls through Meaning projectileDamage int yes Damage on hit. projectileHitPause int yes Hit-stop frames on hit. projectileHitSoundName string yes Sound on hit, base file name without extension. projectileHitSoundPack string yes Pack owning that sound. projectileHitSoundChannel int yes Audio channel slot. Sounds ¶ Playable entities may declare playerUpdateScript (runs before the controller in every animation), specialMoveScript (special eligibility and entry cost), and invincibleOffensiveSpecial (invulnerability on offensive-special entry). These fields apply to the entity itself, without reference fallback. The special hook must explicitly return true ; it replaces the native health gate and later health deduction. See Lua scripting for the hook contract and scripted cancel entry. sounds is a DefaultSoundsData : a packName plus sixteen named groups. Each group is an array of base sound file names without extension; the runtime picks one at random each time. A null group falls through to the reference entity. Groups: jump , landing , quake , attack , weaponThrow , jumpAttack , blitz , defspecial , offspecial , grabMove1 , grabMove2 , grabMove3 , death , run , lowHealth , lastLifeDeath . "sounds": { "packName": "My Pack", "attack": ["punch-a", "punch-b"], "death": ["scream"] } aiData ¶ A raw two-dimensional enemy AI table imported from the ROM. Hand-authoring is not supported. Copy it from a reference entity, or leave it out and let the logic reference supply it. Animation logic ¶ animationsLogic is an array parallel to animations.json animations . Index i describes animation i . Entries may be null , and the array may be shorter than the animation list. Field Type Meaning duration int Logic length of the animation in game frames. hitboxes array Attack boxes active during frame windows. bodyBoxes array Per-frame hurt volumes overriding globalBodyBox . throwLogic object or null Grab and throw choreography. For moving or aerial throws, throwLogic.relativeToAttacker: true anchors victim offsets to the attacker's current position and height for both enemy and player victims. It omits the legacy front/back grab-distance addition. Author the offsets with the usual victim-facing X sign and set useLegacyHardcodedMechanics: false . The default remains false, preserving existing pack choreography. | events | array | Frame-bound logic events. | | script | object or null | Lua script run every frame of this animation. | | referenceBehaviour | object or null | Classic move controller to borrow. | Events override borrowed behaviour If events is non-empty, the animation runs its events plus the default physics step and skips the referenced Classic move controller entirely . This is deliberate: it stops original mode side effects — forced mode changes, timers, hard-coded spawns, damage transitions — from leaking into a custom event-driven animation. A script still runs either way; referenceBehaviour and Classic fallback only apply to animations without events. animationsLogic[i].name also appears in files the Character Editor writes. It is a mirror of the matching animations.json name, kept for readability, and the runtime ignores it. Hitboxes ¶ Field Type Meaning frame int First animation frame the box is active on. duration int Frames it stays active. hitBox {x, y, width, height} int Geometry in pixels relative to the entity pivot. Mirrored automatically when facing left. damage int Damage on hit. knockDown bool Send the victim into the knocked-down state. hitBackwards bool Push the victim away from the attacker's back rather than its front. hitPause int Hit-stop frames applied to both parties. hitEachTargetOnce bool While the hitbox stays active, strike each target once, on any frame (up to four). Without it, once the hitbox connects it skips anyone this character hit last, until the hitbox changes. soundName string Sound on connect, base name without extension. packName string Pack owning that sound. channel int Audio channel slot. soundId int Classic sound slot used when soundName is empty. At most one hitbox is active at a time. They are scanned in array order, so keep them ordered by frame and non-overlapping. Body boxes ¶ Field Type Meaning frame int First animation frame. duration int Frames active. boundingBox BoundingBox Hurt volume for that window. Outside every body box window, globalBodyBox applies. Throw logic ¶ Field Type Meaning offsets array Keyframes placing the held opponent. releaseVelocity {x, y} int Velocity given to the opponent on release. x is whole pixels per frame, pushed towards the victim's own back. y is raw 16.16 fixed point (65536 per pixel), negative is up: -180224 is 2.75 px per frame upward. Not the 1/1000 unit used by VelocityEvent . releaseDamage int Damage applied when the thrown opponent lands . useLegacyHardcodedMechanics bool Index the offsets by the victim's animation tick and ignore opponentFrame , as every ROM throw does. When false the thrower's tick indexes the offsets and opponentFrame freezes the victim on that tick. It does not skip the offsets. Each offset ( OffsetData ): Field Type Meaning frame int Animation tick (game frames elapsed, not image index) the placement applies from. offset {x, y} int Opponent placement in pixels. Negative y is up. x is mirrored so that negative is in front of the opponent. opponentAnimation int Animation id forced on the opponent every frame. Leaving it 0 forces Standing; use the victim slots 18-23 described in Classic Game Mechanics . opponentFrame int Tick the opponent's animation is held at while this keyframe is active. Only used when useLegacyHardcodedMechanics is false . opponentFacesSameDirection bool Face the opponent the same way as the holder rather than towards it. Negative frame values appear in some existing files, left behind by editor frame-shift operations. They never match a real frame and are dead data. Scripts ¶ "script": { "packName": "My Pack", "scriptName": "Block" } scriptName resolves to Scripts/<scriptName>.lua inside packName . The .lua extension is optional and appended when missing. See Lua Scripting . At the root of logic.json , playable entities may set hudScript to draw pack-owned sprites beside their own health bar. It runs in a separate, view-only Lua VM and receives copied player state. Items may set pickupScript ; it runs when a player attempts to collect the item. Returning true consumes the item; returning false or failing leaves it on the ground. Unknown custom items with no pickupScript are ignored. Neither field is inherited from a logic reference. See Custom HUD and pickups . A weapon item may set "throwOnlyWeapon": true at the root of its logic.json . It is then only thrown, like the Classic grenade: a player's attack throws it instead of swinging or stabbing with it, whatever weapon it references (a pepper bottle that references the Classic Knife, for example). The flag is read from the item's own logic, not inherited from a logic reference. Scripts read it as is_throw_only_weapon . Two more weapon options, also read from the item's own logic only: "meleeOnlyWeapon": true : the weapon is never thrown. A player's throw inputs act as if it could not be thrown: the back attack inputs make a back attack, the pick up button drops it. Scripts read it as is_melee_only_weapon . "brokenWeapon": { "packName": ..., "entityName": ... } : on its first hit in a weapon attack the held item becomes that entity, still in the same hand, and the weapon's breakSound plays (a bottle that cracks into a broken bottle). Native characters break it from their weapon attack; scripted ones call break_held_weapon() after a hit. Scripts read it as is_breakable_weapon . "breakSound": { "packName": ..., "soundName": ... } also names the sound a container item plays when it breaks open, in place of the referenced Classic container's. What kind of weapon an item is comes from the Classic weapon it references: Knife , Kunai , Pipe , Sword or Grenade . The native weapon attack and throw use it, and scripts read it as classic_name . Scripts that give weapons their own moves should test classic_name (with is_throw_only_weapon and is_breakable_weapon ) rather than the item's name , so that every pack's knife counts as a knife: the Streets of Rage 1 knife is SOR1 item 08 , a baseball bat or a plank references the Classic Pipe. On a character, the weapon throw animation (slot 44) runs the native throw, which releases the weapon at the tick the referenced Classic character releases it: Axel 7, Blaze 12, Skate 5, others 9. A character whose throw has other art or timing sets "weaponThrowFrame" on that animationsLogic entry to the animation tick of its release. 0 keeps the Classic tick. Reference behaviour ¶ "referenceBehaviour": { "packName": "Classic", "type": 0, "animationId": 0, "objectMode": 2 } objectMode is a move controller mode value: for players and enemies it is controller index * 2 ; for items it is (controller index + 1) * 2 . type is the reference entity's type hash within the pack. The full tables are in Behaviour Modes . Logic events ¶ Each entry in events is an object with a $type and that type's own fields. The editor display names are mapped to these class names in Logic Events . $type must read exactly Sor2NewEra.Gameplay.<ClassName>, Sor2NewEra . Most events fire on a single frame . Some instead watch a window with afterFrame and beforeFrame , where beforeFrame of 0 means no upper bound. A few watch continuously from an initialFrame . Movement ¶ $type class Fields Effect VelocityEvent frame , velocity {x,y,z} , useAxisFlags , affectX , affectY , affectZ Set velocity. Without useAxisFlags , a zero component still overwrites that axis; with it, only the flagged axes are touched. AccelerationEvent frame , acceleration {x,y,z} , useAxisFlags , affectX , affectY , affectZ Set acceleration, same axis rules. InputVelocityEvent strength {x,y} , afterFrame , beforeFrame Apply stick-driven velocity during a window. InputAccelerationEvent strength {x,y} Apply stick-driven acceleration on every frame of the animation. PositionOffsetEvent frame , offset {x,y,z} Teleport, in pixels. x mirrors with facing, z moves on the depth axis. y is added to the depth velocity, not to height; use VelocityEvent for vertical motion. StopEvent frame Stop movement. StopOnHorizontalStop none Stop once horizontal motion ends. On the axis vectors, x is horizontal, y is vertical (the jump axis), and z is depth. Animation flow ¶ $type class Fields Effect JumpToAnimationEvent frame , animationId , animationFrame Switch to another animation. JumpToAnimationOnInputButton input , animationId , afterFrame , beforeFrame Switch when a button is pressed during the window. input is an InputButtons flag value. JumpToAnimationOnInputCombo input , animationId , afterFrame , beforeFrame Switch when a button chain is entered. input is a string, one character per step. JumpToAnimationOnHit animationId , afterFrame , beforeFrame Switch when this entity's attack connects. JumpToAnimationOnLanding initialFrame , animationId , animationFrame Switch on landing. JumpToFrameOnLanding initialFrame , jumpFrame Jump within the same animation on landing. JumpToFrameOnHorizontalStop initialFrame , jumpFrame Jump within the same animation once horizontal motion ends. animationId is the array index in animations.json , the same index used everywhere else. Combo notation for JumpToAnimationOnInputCombo : one character per step, matched in order. ^ up, v down, < left, > right, and a b c x y z for the face buttons. Parsed case-insensitively. Left and right mirror with facing, so a combo written facing right works facing left. "v>a" is down, forward, A. Spawning and interaction ¶ $type class Fields Effect SpawnEnemyEvent frame , packName , entityName , animationId , mode Spawn an enemy. SpawnItemEvent frame , packName , entityName , animationId , mode , lifetime , positionOffset , velocity , isProjectile , damage , hitPause , hitSoundName , hitSoundPack , hitSoundChannel Spawn an item, optionally as a damaging projectile. This is how fireballs are built. GrabEvent frame Grab the character this entity is currently attacking. FlipEvent frame Reverse facing. DestroyEvent frame Destroy this entity. SpawnItemEvent positionOffset and velocity are in internal position units, not pixels: about 65.5 units per pixel, +x forward, +y up, so editor-written values are typically in the thousands. lifetime of 0 means 60 frames , not "never expire". See Classic Game Mechanics . State ¶ $type class Fields Effect InvincibilityEvent frame , invincible Turn invincibility on or off. Always pair the two. HealthEvent frame , health Add health. Negative subtracts, which is how special-move self-damage is authored. SetCustomValueEvent frame , valueId , value Write a custom value slot, readable and writable from Lua. Audio ¶ $type class Fields Effect SoundEvent frame , packName , soundName , soundNames , channel Play a sound. soundNames is a random pool and takes precedence over soundName when non-empty. MusicEvent frame , packName , musicName Change the music track. channel decides which audio slot the sound occupies. Sounds on the same slot cut each other off, so use different slots for sounds that should overlap. 0 sfx, 1 sfxBgm, 2 voice and 3 prioritary are the named slots, but the runtime treats the value as a plain index and allocates as many slots as it sees, so any non-negative number is a valid private channel. Example ¶ A fireball spawned on frame 40 of animation 47, with a voice line on frame 36: { "duration": 60, "hitboxes": [], "bodyBoxes": [], "events": [ { "$type": "Sor2NewEra.Gameplay.SoundEvent, Sor2NewEra", "frame": 36, "packName": "My Pack", "soundName": "hadoken", "channel": 2 }, { "$type": "Sor2NewEra.Gameplay.SpawnItemEvent, Sor2NewEra", "frame": 40, "packName": "My Pack", "entityName": "Fireball", "animationId": 0, "mode": -1, "lifetime": 0, "positionOffset": { "x": 2750, "y": 2750 }, "velocity": { "x": 250, "y": 0 }, "isProjectile": true, "damage": 30, "hitPause": 6 } ] } dependencies.json ¶ Optional. Declares assets from other packs that this entity needs, so they are loaded and shipped. { "entities": [{ "packName": "Classic", "entityName": "Shiva" }], "sounds": [{ "packName": "Classic", "soundName": "29" }] } The file may also contain a literal null , which the editor writes for an entity with no declared dependencies. That is the same as the file being absent. Related pages ¶ Logic Events for editor names. Behaviour Modes for objectMode and referenceBehaviour . Enums and Identifiers for the animation slot table and Classic entity names. Create a Playable Character From Scratch . Classic Game Mechanics for units, throw choreography, running, items, containers and AI as the original game implements them. Visual afterimages ¶ Set afterimages: true on an animationsLogic entry to show recent player poses through the existing Ninpo shadow renderer. This is visual only: it does not enable clone attacks or add collision bodies. Defaults to false, is suppressed during cinematics, and rejects history from another entity or animation. Requires the generic authored-afterimage engine support. Weapon health budgets ¶ logic.weaponHealth > 0 opts a weapon into a health budget instead of Classic's drop counter. weaponDropHealthCost is consumed on landing or swap. animationsLogic[].weaponHealthCost charges on completion if at least one hit connected (misses and interrupted moves do not pay), while hitboxes[].weaponHealthCost charges per connected hitbox; both are independent of damage multipliers. Exhaustion drops the held weapon and its next landing expires it. All counters are in ItemModel , not Lua upvalues, and are restored by rollback. Zero-valued configuration preserves Classic behaviour. Normal attacks without authored wear do not consume health. Lua item.weapon_health reads/writes the rollback health counter, allowing original spawn or container tables to override the default budget. This does not enable the feature on entities whose weaponHealth configuration is zero. weaponContactHealthCost optionally overrides a positive hitbox wear cost using the held weapon's own value. Zero preserves attack-authored costs. Zero-cost hitboxes remain free, and animation-completion fees are unaffected. Use this for weapons whose wear differs even when they share a character move.

docs.text: An entity is a playable character, an enemy, an item, a container, or a piece of scenery. Everything about it lives in one folder: Entities/<Entity Name>/ own content Entity Replacements/Classic/<Entity Name>/ replacement for a Classic entity Both use exactly the same file set. The folder name is the entity name used by every entityName reference. File Required Purpose spriteSettings.json yes How many sprite frames the entity has, and where each one's pivot sits. animations.json yes Which frame is shown for how long, per animation. logic.json yes Gameplay behaviour: stats, boxes, events, scripts. dependencies.json no Declared references to other packs' assets. <i>.png as needed Own sprite frames, zero-based. portrait.png , preview.png no Character select art. Palettes/palette <n>.png no Palette guides for this entity. See Palette Files . Three ideas govern all of it: the sprite index model , the reference fallback model , and the parallel animation arrays . Get these right and the rest is data entry.

docs.text: Everything that names a sprite uses an effective index , and effective indices are not PNG numbers. An entity may borrow another entity's sprite frames by setting referenceEntityPackName and referenceEntityName in spriteSettings.json . When it does, the combined frame list is: index 0 .. R-1 the reference entity's frames, in its own order index R .. R+N-1 this entity's own frames, where own frame k is the file k.png R is the reference entity's total frame count. N is the length of this entity's pivots array. Without a reference, R is 0 and effective index k is simply k.png . This matters in three places: animations.json frames[].imageId is an effective index. spriteSettings.json iconIndex is an effective index. Changing the sprite reference changes R , which shifts every own frame's effective index. The Character Editor remaps imageId values when you change the reference; a hand edit must do the same. pivots defines the frame count, not the files. If pivots has 12 entries, the entity has own frames 0.png through 11.png . A 12.png sitting in the folder is invisible. A missing 7.png with a pivot at index 7 is a frame that draws nothing.

"sounds": { "packName": "My Pack", "attack": ["punch-a", "punch-b"], "death": ["scream"] }
docs.title: Sounds

docs.text: A raw two-dimensional enemy AI table imported from the ROM. Hand-authoring is not supported. Copy it from a reference entity, or leave it out and let the logic reference supply it.
docs.title: aiData

docs.text: animationsLogic is an array parallel to animations.json animations . Index i describes animation i . Entries may be null , and the array may be shorter than the animation list. Field Type Meaning duration int Logic length of the animation in game frames. hitboxes array Attack boxes active during frame windows. bodyBoxes array Per-frame hurt volumes overriding globalBodyBox . throwLogic object or null Grab and throw choreography. For moving or aerial throws, throwLogic.relativeToAttacker: true anchors victim offsets to the attacker's current position and height for both enemy and player victims. It omits the legacy front/back grab-distance addition. Author the offsets with the usual victim-facing X sign and set useLegacyHardcodedMechanics: false . The default remains false, preserving existing pack choreography. | events | array | Frame-bound logic events. | | script | object or null | Lua script run every frame of this animation. | | referenceBehaviour | object or null | Classic move controller to borrow. | Events override borrowed behaviour If events is non-empty, the animation runs its events plus the default physics step and skips the referenced Classic move controller entirely . This is deliberate: it stops original mode side effects — forced mode changes, timers, hard-coded spawns, damage transitions — from leaking into a custom event-driven animation. A script still runs either way; referenceBehaviour and Classic fallback only apply to animations without events. animationsLogic[i].name also appears in files the Character Editor writes. It is a mirror of the matching animations.json name, kept for readability, and the runtime ignores it.
docs.title: Animation logic

docs.text: Field Type Meaning frame int First animation frame the box is active on. duration int Frames it stays active. hitBox {x, y, width, height} int Geometry in pixels relative to the entity pivot. Mirrored automatically when facing left. damage int Damage on hit. knockDown bool Send the victim into the knocked-down state. hitBackwards bool Push the victim away from the attacker's back rather than its front. hitPause int Hit-stop frames applied to both parties. hitEachTargetOnce bool While the hitbox stays active, strike each target once, on any frame (up to four). Without it, once the hitbox connects it skips anyone this character hit last, until the hitbox changes. soundName string Sound on connect, base name without extension. packName string Pack owning that sound. channel int Audio channel slot. soundId int Classic sound slot used when soundName is empty. At most one hitbox is active at a time. They are scanned in array order, so keep them ordered by frame and non-overlapping.
docs.title: Hitboxes

docs.text: Field Type Meaning frame int First animation frame. duration int Frames active. boundingBox BoundingBox Hurt volume for that window. Outside every body box window, globalBodyBox applies.
docs.title: Body boxes

docs.text: Field Type Meaning offsets array Keyframes placing the held opponent. releaseVelocity {x, y} int Velocity given to the opponent on release. x is whole pixels per frame, pushed towards the victim's own back. y is raw 16.16 fixed point (65536 per pixel), negative is up: -180224 is 2.75 px per frame upward. Not the 1/1000 unit used by VelocityEvent . releaseDamage int Damage applied when the thrown opponent lands . useLegacyHardcodedMechanics bool Index the offsets by the victim's animation tick and ignore opponentFrame , as every ROM throw does. When false the thrower's tick indexes the offsets and opponentFrame freezes the victim on that tick. It does not skip the offsets. Each offset ( OffsetData ): Field Type Meaning frame int Animation tick (game frames elapsed, not image index) the placement applies from. offset {x, y} int Opponent placement in pixels. Negative y is up. x is mirrored so that negative is in front of the opponent. opponentAnimation int Animation id forced on the opponent every frame. Leaving it 0 forces Standing; use the victim slots 18-23 described in Classic Game Mechanics . opponentFrame int Tick the opponent's animation is held at while this keyframe is active. Only used when useLegacyHardcodedMechanics is false . opponentFacesSameDirection bool Face the opponent the same way as the holder rather than towards it. Negative frame values appear in some existing files, left behind by editor frame-shift operations. They never match a real frame and are dead data.
docs.title: Throw logic

docs.text: "script": { "packName": "My Pack", "scriptName": "Block" } scriptName resolves to Scripts/<scriptName>.lua inside packName . The .lua extension is optional and appended when missing. See Lua Scripting . At the root of logic.json , playable entities may set hudScript to draw pack-owned sprites beside their own health bar. It runs in a separate, view-only Lua VM and receives copied player state. Items may set pickupScript ; it runs when a player attempts to collect the item. Returning true consumes the item; returning false or failing leaves it on the ground. Unknown custom items with no pickupScript are ignored. Neither field is inherited from a logic reference. See Custom HUD and pickups . A weapon item may set "throwOnlyWeapon": true at the root of its logic.json . It is then only thrown, like the Classic grenade: a player's attack throws it instead of swinging or stabbing with it, whatever weapon it references (a pepper bottle that references the Classic Knife, for example). The flag is read from the item's own logic, not inherited from a logic reference. Scripts read it as is_throw_only_weapon . Two more weapon options, also read from the item's own logic only: "meleeOnlyWeapon": true : the weapon is never thrown. A player's throw inputs act as if it could not be thrown: the back attack inputs make a back attack, the pick up button drops it. Scripts read it as is_melee_only_weapon . "brokenWeapon": { "packName": ..., "entityName": ... } : on its first hit in a weapon attack the held item becomes that entity, still in the same hand, and the weapon's breakSound plays (a bottle that cracks into a broken bottle). Native characters break it from their weapon attack; scripted ones call break_held_weapon() after a hit. Scripts read it as is_breakable_weapon . "breakSound": { "packName": ..., "soundName": ... } also names the sound a container item plays when it breaks open, in place of the referenced Classic container's. What kind of weapon an item is comes from the Classic weapon it references: Knife , Kunai , Pipe , Sword or Grenade . The native weapon attack and throw use it, and scripts read it as classic_name . Scripts that give weapons their own moves should test classic_name (with is_throw_only_weapon and is_breakable_weapon ) rather than the item's name , so that every pack's knife counts as a knife: the Streets of Rage 1 knife is SOR1 item 08 , a baseball bat or a plank references the Classic Pipe. On a character, the weapon throw animation (slot 44) runs the native throw, which releases the weapon at the tick the referenced Classic character releases it: Axel 7, Blaze 12, Skate 5, others 9. A character whose throw has other art or timing sets "weaponThrowFrame" on that animationsLogic entry to the animation tick of its release. 0 keeps the Classic tick.
docs.title: Scripts

docs.text: "referenceBehaviour": { "packName": "Classic", "type": 0, "animationId": 0, "objectMode": 2 } objectMode is a move controller mode value: for players and enemies it is controller index * 2 ; for items it is (controller index + 1) * 2 . type is the reference entity's type hash within the pack. The full tables are in Behaviour Modes .
docs.title: Reference behaviour

docs.text: Each entry in events is an object with a $type and that type's own fields. The editor display names are mapped to these class names in Logic Events . $type must read exactly Sor2NewEra.Gameplay.<ClassName>, Sor2NewEra . Most events fire on a single frame . Some instead watch a window with afterFrame and beforeFrame , where beforeFrame of 0 means no upper bound. A few watch continuously from an initialFrame .
docs.title: Logic events

docs.text: $type class Fields Effect VelocityEvent frame , velocity {x,y,z} , useAxisFlags , affectX , affectY , affectZ Set velocity. Without useAxisFlags , a zero component still overwrites that axis; with it, only the flagged axes are touched. AccelerationEvent frame , acceleration {x,y,z} , useAxisFlags , affectX , affectY , affectZ Set acceleration, same axis rules. InputVelocityEvent strength {x,y} , afterFrame , beforeFrame Apply stick-driven velocity during a window. InputAccelerationEvent strength {x,y} Apply stick-driven acceleration on every frame of the animation. PositionOffsetEvent frame , offset {x,y,z} Teleport, in pixels. x mirrors with facing, z moves on the depth axis. y is added to the depth velocity, not to height; use VelocityEvent for vertical motion. StopEvent frame Stop movement. StopOnHorizontalStop none Stop once horizontal motion ends. On the axis vectors, x is horizontal, y is vertical (the jump axis), and z is depth.
docs.title: Movement

docs.text: $type class Fields Effect JumpToAnimationEvent frame , animationId , animationFrame Switch to another animation. JumpToAnimationOnInputButton input , animationId , afterFrame , beforeFrame Switch when a button is pressed during the window. input is an InputButtons flag value. JumpToAnimationOnInputCombo input , animationId , afterFrame , beforeFrame Switch when a button chain is entered. input is a string, one character per step. JumpToAnimationOnHit animationId , afterFrame , beforeFrame Switch when this entity's attack connects. JumpToAnimationOnLanding initialFrame , animationId , animationFrame Switch on landing. JumpToFrameOnLanding initialFrame , jumpFrame Jump within the same animation on landing. JumpToFrameOnHorizontalStop initialFrame , jumpFrame Jump within the same animation once horizontal motion ends. animationId is the array index in animations.json , the same index used everywhere else. Combo notation for JumpToAnimationOnInputCombo : one character per step, matched in order. ^ up, v down, < left, > right, and a b c x y z for the face buttons. Parsed case-insensitively. Left and right mirror with facing, so a combo written facing right works facing left. "v>a" is down, forward, A.
docs.title: Animation flow

docs.text: $type class Fields Effect SpawnEnemyEvent frame , packName , entityName , animationId , mode Spawn an enemy. SpawnItemEvent frame , packName , entityName , animationId , mode , lifetime , positionOffset , velocity , isProjectile , damage , hitPause , hitSoundName , hitSoundPack , hitSoundChannel Spawn an item, optionally as a damaging projectile. This is how fireballs are built. GrabEvent frame Grab the character this entity is currently attacking. FlipEvent frame Reverse facing. DestroyEvent frame Destroy this entity. SpawnItemEvent positionOffset and velocity are in internal position units, not pixels: about 65.5 units per pixel, +x forward, +y up, so editor-written values are typically in the thousands. lifetime of 0 means 60 frames , not "never expire". See Classic Game Mechanics .
docs.title: Spawning and interaction

docs.text: $type class Fields Effect InvincibilityEvent frame , invincible Turn invincibility on or off. Always pair the two. HealthEvent frame , health Add health. Negative subtracts, which is how special-move self-damage is authored. SetCustomValueEvent frame , valueId , value Write a custom value slot, readable and writable from Lua.
docs.title: State

docs.text: $type class Fields Effect SoundEvent frame , packName , soundName , soundNames , channel Play a sound. soundNames is a random pool and takes precedence over soundName when non-empty. MusicEvent frame , packName , musicName Change the music track. channel decides which audio slot the sound occupies. Sounds on the same slot cut each other off, so use different slots for sounds that should overlap. 0 sfx, 1 sfxBgm, 2 voice and 3 prioritary are the named slots, but the runtime treats the value as a plain index and allocates as many slots as it sees, so any non-negative number is a valid private channel.
docs.title: Audio

docs.text: A fireball spawned on frame 40 of animation 47, with a voice line on frame 36: { "duration": 60, "hitboxes": [], "bodyBoxes": [], "events": [ { "$type": "Sor2NewEra.Gameplay.SoundEvent, Sor2NewEra", "frame": 36, "packName": "My Pack", "soundName": "hadoken", "channel": 2 }, { "$type": "Sor2NewEra.Gameplay.SpawnItemEvent, Sor2NewEra", "frame": 40, "packName": "My Pack", "entityName": "Fireball", "animationId": 0, "mode": -1, "lifetime": 0, "positionOffset": { "x": 2750, "y": 2750 }, "velocity": { "x": 250, "y": 0 }, "isProjectile": true, "damage": 30, "hitPause": 6 } ] }
docs.title: Example

docs.text: Optional. Declares assets from other packs that this entity needs, so they are loaded and shipped. { "entities": [{ "packName": "Classic", "entityName": "Shiva" }], "sounds": [{ "packName": "Classic", "soundName": "29" }] } The file may also contain a literal null , which the editor writes for an entity with no declared dependencies. That is the same as the file being absent.
docs.title: dependencies.json
