docs.text: Scripted stages ¶ game.custom_value_1 through game.custom_value_16 are signed integers in GameModel. They are included in rollback snapshots, start at zero for a new game and persist across scene/level transitions. Reserve slots centrally across the mod and its dependencies. Do not store gameplay state in Lua globals or upvalues. A scene's updateScript: {packName, scriptName} runs once per simulation update, after emulated-lag rejection and before entity updates. It has no current entity. Use game.get_player etc. It does not run during entrance/exit transitions. While a gameplay cinematic runs, the scene's simulation is frozen but its art keeps animating: frame (the global timer that clocks layer visual scripts and palette cycles) keeps counting. The update script is skipped, unless the scene sets updateScriptDuringCinematics: true : it then also runs on each cinematic update, after the cinematic script, with game.is_cinematic true. That run is for presentation only (a bobbing camera Y, the custom values that drive layer visual scripts): game.spawn_scene_enemy and game.spawn_scene_item return -1 in it, and the script must leave its own progress (clocks, spawn streams) alone until game.is_cinematic is false. A camera_y it writes overrides the cinematic script's, and is the one kept when the cinematic ends (the camera X still returns to where the cinematic started). postUpdateScript uses the same reference format and runs once after entity animation and native weapon attachment placement at the end of a completed gameplay update. It has no current entity. Use it when placement depends on the final animation frame; its return value is ignored. enterScript has the same reference format. It runs once after native player placement, before enemies spawn. Set scriptedEntrance: true when that script owns placement: this preserves the fade delay without walking the players back to the Classic starting positions. Reset per-visit timers in this hook, not in Lua globals. The update hook's return value is ignored. scriptedProgression: true disables automatic wave/scene advancement and the engine's automatic GO prompts. The script owns encounter boundaries and may call game.schedule_go_forward_effect() between encounters. Call game.change_scene(zeroBasedSceneIndex) to enter any scene in the current level. It returns false for an invalid index; on success, return from the script immediately. The next update uses normal scene initialization, clearing enemies and unheld items, resetting spawn cursors, and running enterScript . Use this from the scene update hook. game.scene_enemies_cleared checks both remaining loadcues and active enemies, including the spawn delay, so a gap between two waves is not mistaken for scene completion. For a normal forward transition, call game.complete_scene() and return from the script. It enters the scene's sceneExitCodeId strategy (walking/fade or stage clear), then the next scene's normal entrance. It returns false outside active gameplay, so repeated calls cannot restart a transition. Use this instead of advance_wave() or advance_level() when the exit presentation must play. A physical scene may contain several scripted camera-lock waves. Declare scriptedWaveCount and scriptedWaveCustomValue (1–16) to expose those waves in the custom-game menu. Starting at a selected wave seeds that game custom value with a one-based wave index before the entrance script. The script must honor that seed for a new game, position the camera/player and skip earlier spawns. Ordinary transitions should reset the index to the first wave. Zero/default counts retain one wave per scene. This does not create extra physical scenes; existing scene selection IDs and replays retain their original meanings. scriptedEnemies: true disables automatic enemy cues for that scene. Use game.spawn_scene_enemy(index) to instantiate one zero-based enemies1 cue through native enemy initialization. It returns the enemy object ID, or -1 if invalid or all slots are occupied. It does not advance cue cursors or recursively spawn later cues. The script must retry a failed spawn and record started/cleared encounters in snapshot variables. In these scenes scene_enemies_cleared means no active enemies; future scripted encounters do not prevent the current area from unlocking. Ordinary scenes retain the full cue/delay completion check above. The custom game settings apply to scripted spawns without any work from the script. Settings that act on the enemy as a whole wait until the update that spawned it has finished, so they see the health, custom values and position the script left on the enemy: Enemies health multiplier: applied to the health the script set, extra bars included (the script's bar size is kept). It is applied at the end of the frame in which the enemy's AI script first owns an update, so health set by a stage spawn routine or by the enemy's own AI on its first tick is both covered; an enemy without an AI script is done on its spawn frame. Health an AI rewrites later (a formation breaking up, a phase change) is the script's own. Enemy count multiplier: every spawn is duplicated as an exact copy of the configured enemy (custom values, health, position nudged sideways), so a Lua driven enemy's double runs the same behaviour. Copies take enemy slots like any spawn and are skipped when none is free. Bosses are doubled too, all at once with their source, and a copy of an enemy flagged is_boss is a boss as well: as with native bosses, only the last boss down runs the boss finale (the death controller drops is_boss from the others as they fall). A boss script with its own post-defeat sequence (an escape, a death scene that ends the stage) should run it only when no other boss is still alive, and a stage that waits for its boss should look for any live is_boss enemy rather than one slot. Copies are extra to the stage's pacing, like native doubles are extra to the loadcues: number_of_alive_enemies leaves them out (so "spawn the next one when N are left" sees only the stage's own enemies), except that it never reads 0 while a copy is still alive, so a wave still ends only once the copies are down. The sideways nudge alternates sides while the source is on screen, but never puts a copy further outside the view than its source: copies of an enemy placed ahead of the view (a resident that wakes when the screen reaches it) sit between it and the view, never beyond an area barrier the camera stops at. More enemies also means more drops: every item slot can be taken, so a stage that places scenery or weapons with spawn_scene_item should not let a failed item spawn hold back its enemy spawns. Randomizer (Royal / Swaps / Shuffle): a non-boss spawn may be re-typed as another of the pack's own enemy kinds, picked from every entity the pack's levels spawn outside a boss slot. Everything else the spawn set (health, custom values, spawn record) stays, and the new kind's own AI takes over; its display name and palette become the new kind's. Knockouts re-types a knocked out enemy the same way. "Spawns" only rolls Classic entrances and leaves custom packs alone. A pack whose enemies depend on their cue (a scripted entrance, a weapon spawned for that kind) should expect the new kind to arrive with the old kind's record. Enemies velocity multiplier: applied when a script owned move is integrated ( velocity_x / velocity_y left on an enemy by its AI, or an explicit update_position_and_check_world_collisions() call). The stored velocity is unchanged afterwards. Positions a script writes directly are not scaled. A script that spawns or moves its enemies itself, outside engine spawns and velocity integration, reads enemies_multiplier , enemies_velocity_numerator and enemies_velocity_denominator and applies them on its own (TwinBee lengthens its waves and scales each enemy's per-tick movement). They come from the session, so every netplay peer reads the same values; read them every tick instead of storing them. Instant spawns: scripted stages pace their own spawns, so read game.has_instant_spawns and drop the delays yourself. Damage multipliers, infighting, killer, exploding and Ninpo enemies act on the native hit and death handling and need nothing from the script. The exception is killer mode's attack timing for an enemy whose script writes its animation frames itself: see Killer Mode . The engine's own "GO!" prompt (shown when no enemy is left and the scene can still scroll, then every 15 seconds, or after 5 seconds without enemies) waits 5 seconds after a stage or scene start, including advance_wave() and change_scene() , before its first appearance. In a scriptedEnemies scene this gives the script time to spawn its first enemies; call schedule_go_forward_effect() to show it yourself. scriptedItems: true disables automatic item cues. Use game.spawn_scene_item(index) to spawn one zero-based items cue through native initialization, including container contents and flags. It bypasses the camera filter and does not advance any cue cursor. It returns the object ID, or -1 for an invalid cue or exhausted pool; retry a failed allocation. A cue with status bit 7 uses a sub-item slot. Record successful allocations in snapshot state. preloadItems: true spawns item cues without the normal one-way camera-position filter, so switches behind the starting camera still exist when players backtrack. Available item slots still limit simultaneous objects; keep the fixture count bounded. scriptedClock: true disables the normal HUD countdown and its time-out damage. Use game.set_clock(integer) and implement the desired consequences in the simulation hook. game.difficulty_index is the zero-based configuration index; game.screen_width is the current playable width in pixels. game.enemy_capacity is the active enemy-slot count; enemy object IDs start at 4. Set game.scripted_camera = true to disable automatic scrolling. Set game.camera_x and game.camera_y in viewport pixels, positive right/down. Collision, spawning and rendering read that same camera state. Scripts must choose bounds and multiplayer framing; the engine does not clamp the camera. Rendering follows scripted cameras smoothly in both horizontal directions. Clear scripted_camera to restore normal scrolling. Scene entrance resets it. Lua numbers in this engine are 32-bit integers , not floating point. Like every script, a stage hook returns its update function, which the engine calls on every update (see Script structure ). Camera pixels and entity bridge coordinates use different units: a pixel coordinate converts to an entity position using (pixels * 65536 + 500) / 1000 (integer division). For example, a camera stationary at pixel 500: return function() game.scripted_camera = true game.camera_x = 500 game.camera_y = 0 game.custom_value_1 = game.custom_value_1 + 1 return false end Indexed tile layers ¶ An art layer's tilemap contains width , height , tiles , cells , palette and optional paletteCycles and scale . Tiles are base64 4bpp: 32 bytes per 8x8 tile, rows top-to-bottom, high nibble first. Cells are row-major 16-bit Genesis words: bits 0..10 tile index, 11 horizontal flip, 12 vertical flip, 13..14 palette line, 15 foreground priority. palette contains 64 Genesis 0BGR color words. Index zero of each line is transparent. Layer position is the top-left origin; scale (default 1) multiplies the layer's size around that origin, for art authored at a different resolution. The engine accepts 1..2048 tiles, maps up to 2048x2048 cells, and even-channel Genesis color words ( color & ~0xEEE == 0 ). A color of -1 is transparent, like index zero: palette cycles can use it to hide and reveal pixels, for example a dissolve whose frames turn indices on one after another. Invalid tile references, palette lengths, and palette cycle ranges are rejected. tools/validate_mod.py checks these constraints and scene/layer script references before loading the mod. Priority tiles render 16 world Z units ahead of the layer: a layer at Z=10 places its priority tiles at Z=-6, matching the native foreground convention. Each cycle is {startIndex, ticksPerFrame, frames} . Frames are equal-length arrays of replacement color words. Cycles derive their phase from the simulation timer, so rollback and pause do not drift the phase. Later overlapping cycles win. Optional preserveInitialPalette: true keeps the authored base colors before ticksPerFrame ; the first boundary then selects frame one (normal cycle phase). The default applies frame zero immediately. The packed art is included directly in exported JSON; no runtime ROM is needed. Visual scripts ¶ A layer's visualScript: {packName, scriptName} uses a separate VM with no gameplay bridge. It receives only a copied visual table: frame , simulation_frame , camera_x , camera_y , level_id , scene_id , live_level_id , custom_values[1..16] , quake_force , quake_force_milli , quake_skip_frames , quake_sequence . The milli value retains fractional quake strength as an integer multiplied by 1000. frame is the gameplay timer; simulation_frame is the viewed simulation frame and continues during scene entry/exit transitions. Use simulation_frame for continuously animated scenery. It stays fixed when simulation is paused and follows rollback; it is not a wall-clock or render-frame counter. A delivered quake increments the sequence; cancellation clears its force. As with gameplay scripts, the chunk runs once and returns an update function, which the view calls every frame. That function returns a table containing optional offset_x , offset_y (pixels, positive right/up), offset_x_milli , offset_y_milli (thousandths of a pixel, added to the pixel offsets: Lua numbers are integers, so this is how a layer moves by sub-pixel steps), visible , palette_tick to override the palette clock (for example, starting gas colors when an alarm activates), and, for a tilemap layer, first_cell and cell_count : only the cells first_cell to first_cell + cell_count - 1 , counted row-major from zero, are drawn (by default all). A typewriter reveals its text by growing cell_count ; a strip of tile variants shows one of them with cell_count = 1 and an offset_x that moves it into place. The visual table is the same object on every call, refilled before each one. When none of its values changed since the previous call (several render frames on one simulation frame, a pause), the function is not called and its previous result stays: it must return the same result for the same inputs, so keep counters in the inputs, never in the script. level_id and scene_id are those of the art being shown: while a cinematic shows another scene's art ( set_cinematic_presentation ), they are that scene's. live_level_id is always the live fight's level, whose entities are the ones on screen: a layer can use it to draw, in a borrowed scene, what that scene's own items would have drawn. In a cutscene (including ending screens) there is no game state: frame counts frames since that cutscene scene started, custom_values are all zero, and tilemap palette cycles follow the same clock. A cutscene built from tilemaps and visual scripts loads at once: its art is in the JSON and no image files are read. The Streets of Rage 1 campaign's ending is an example: its planes and sprites are tilemap layers, its palette fades are palette-cycle frames, and its scripts pick the frame, the position and the credits text cells from frame . Visual scripts cannot mutate health, collision, RNG or stage flow. Prefer effects derived from frame/snapshot values. Rollback may redeliver visual quake events; never use visual state for gameplay decisions. -- An alarm selected by rollback state, with a palette clock starting at zero. return function() return { visible = visual.custom_values[2] ~= 0, palette_tick = visual.frame - visual.custom_values[3] } end The visual VM deliberately has no game , IO, OS or CLR access, and like the gameplay sandbox no math library (numbers are 32-bit integers). Its scratch state is not serialized. Gameplay hooks must derive all persistent state from the game/entity model; a visual hook must never be used to decide gameplay. GameModel layout changes require matching engine builds for replays/netplay.

Lua numbers in this engine are 32-bit integers , not floating point. Like every script, a stage hook returns its update function, which the engine calls on every update (see Script structure ). Camera pixels and entity bridge coordinates use different units: a pixel coordinate converts to an entity position using (pixels * 65536 + 500) / 1000 (integer division). For example, a camera stationary at pixel 500: return function() game.scripted_camera = true game.camera_x = 500 game.camera_y = 0 game.custom_value_1 = game.custom_value_1 + 1 return false end
docs.title: Scripted stages

docs.text: An art layer's tilemap contains width , height , tiles , cells , palette and optional paletteCycles and scale . Tiles are base64 4bpp: 32 bytes per 8x8 tile, rows top-to-bottom, high nibble first. Cells are row-major 16-bit Genesis words: bits 0..10 tile index, 11 horizontal flip, 12 vertical flip, 13..14 palette line, 15 foreground priority. palette contains 64 Genesis 0BGR color words. Index zero of each line is transparent. Layer position is the top-left origin; scale (default 1) multiplies the layer's size around that origin, for art authored at a different resolution. The engine accepts 1..2048 tiles, maps up to 2048x2048 cells, and even-channel Genesis color words ( color & ~0xEEE == 0 ). A color of -1 is transparent, like index zero: palette cycles can use it to hide and reveal pixels, for example a dissolve whose frames turn indices on one after another. Invalid tile references, palette lengths, and palette cycle ranges are rejected. tools/validate_mod.py checks these constraints and scene/layer script references before loading the mod. Priority tiles render 16 world Z units ahead of the layer: a layer at Z=10 places its priority tiles at Z=-6, matching the native foreground convention. Each cycle is {startIndex, ticksPerFrame, frames} . Frames are equal-length arrays of replacement color words. Cycles derive their phase from the simulation timer, so rollback and pause do not drift the phase. Later overlapping cycles win. Optional preserveInitialPalette: true keeps the authored base colors before ticksPerFrame ; the first boundary then selects frame one (normal cycle phase). The default applies frame zero immediately. The packed art is included directly in exported JSON; no runtime ROM is needed.
docs.title: Indexed tile layers

docs.text: A layer's visualScript: {packName, scriptName} uses a separate VM with no gameplay bridge. It receives only a copied visual table: frame , simulation_frame , camera_x , camera_y , level_id , scene_id , live_level_id , custom_values[1..16] , quake_force , quake_force_milli , quake_skip_frames , quake_sequence . The milli value retains fractional quake strength as an integer multiplied by 1000. frame is the gameplay timer; simulation_frame is the viewed simulation frame and continues during scene entry/exit transitions. Use simulation_frame for continuously animated scenery. It stays fixed when simulation is paused and follows rollback; it is not a wall-clock or render-frame counter. A delivered quake increments the sequence; cancellation clears its force. As with gameplay scripts, the chunk runs once and returns an update function, which the view calls every frame. That function returns a table containing optional offset_x , offset_y (pixels, positive right/up), offset_x_milli , offset_y_milli (thousandths of a pixel, added to the pixel offsets: Lua numbers are integers, so this is how a layer moves by sub-pixel steps), visible , palette_tick to override the palette clock (for example, starting gas colors when an alarm activates), and, for a tilemap layer, first_cell and cell_count : only the cells first_cell to first_cell + cell_count - 1 , counted row-major from zero, are drawn (by default all). A typewriter reveals its text by growing cell_count ; a strip of tile variants shows one of them with cell_count = 1 and an offset_x that moves it into place. The visual table is the same object on every call, refilled before each one. When none of its values changed since the previous call (several render frames on one simulation frame, a pause), the function is not called and its previous result stays: it must return the same result for the same inputs, so keep counters in the inputs, never in the script. level_id and scene_id are those of the art being shown: while a cinematic shows another scene's art ( set_cinematic_presentation ), they are that scene's. live_level_id is always the live fight's level, whose entities are the ones on screen: a layer can use it to draw, in a borrowed scene, what that scene's own items would have drawn. In a cutscene (including ending screens) there is no game state: frame counts frames since that cutscene scene started, custom_values are all zero, and tilemap palette cycles follow the same clock. A cutscene built from tilemaps and visual scripts loads at once: its art is in the JSON and no image files are read. The Streets of Rage 1 campaign's ending is an example: its planes and sprites are tilemap layers, its palette fades are palette-cycle frames, and its scripts pick the frame, the position and the credits text cells from frame . Visual scripts cannot mutate health, collision, RNG or stage flow. Prefer effects derived from frame/snapshot values. Rollback may redeliver visual quake events; never use visual state for gameplay decisions. -- An alarm selected by rollback state, with a palette clock starting at zero. return function() return { visible = visual.custom_values[2] ~= 0, palette_tick = visual.frame - visual.custom_values[3] } end The visual VM deliberately has no game , IO, OS or CLR access, and like the gameplay sandbox no math library (numbers are 32-bit integers). Its scratch state is not serialized. Gameplay hooks must derive all persistent state from the game/entity model; a visual hook must never be used to decide gameplay. GameModel layout changes require matching engine builds for replays/netplay.

docs.text: Character API ¶ Character represents shared player and enemy combat behavior. It inherits the Item API and SubItem API , so physics and animation fields are available directly on a character. Identity And Health ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail is_player bool read True for player characters. is_enemy bool read True for enemy characters. display_name string read/write Name shown by UI or combat displays. maximum_health int read/write Maximum health. previous_health int read/write Last recorded health. health int read/write Current health. Setting it also updates visual health for this character. lives int read/write Player lives, or remaining extra health bars for an enemy. An enemy with zero current health can still be alive when this is positive. continues int read/write Continue count where applicable. score int read/write Score, mainly useful for player characters. Combat Links ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail victim Character read Resolved attacked_character_id , or nil . attacker Character read Resolved attacker_character_id , or nil . attacked_character_id int read/write Object ID of the current victim. Use -1 to clear. attacker_character_id int read/write Object ID of the current attacker. Use -1 to clear. previousAttackedCharacterId_1 int read/write Original combo/history slot. Use exact spelling. previousAttackedCharacterId_2 int read/write Original combo/history slot. Use exact spelling. previousAttackedCharacterId_3 int read/write Original combo/history slot. Use exact spelling. last_attacked_character_id int read/write Last attacked character. When changing facing during active attacks, clear stale victim links if the old victim should no longer be treated as connected: local victim = character.victim if victim ~= nil then victim.attacker_character_id = -1 end character.attacked_character_id = -1 Damage, Combo, And State ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail damage_taken int read/write Damage from the last hit. Modify before applying custom health logic. auxiliar_velocity_x int read/write Knocked/thrown auxiliary X velocity. Name follows the bridge. unknownCounter_9A int read/write Original behaviour counter. Use exact spelling. is_static_grab_attack bool read/write Static grab attack state. combo_count int read/write Current combo count. combo_reset_timer int read/write Frames until combo reset. can_advance_combo_count bool read/write Whether combo count can advance. is_hitting_someone bool read/write Character-level hit flag. is_vaulting bool read/write Vaulting over an opponent. run_timer int read/write Run timing state. thrown_hit_count int read/write Count of hits caused while thrown. being_comboed_count int read/write Count used while this character is being comboed. Hit And Grab Methods ¶ Method Returns Detail check_being_hit_or_grabbed() bool Runs hit and grab checks. Player default physics calls this with grab enforcement disabled; enemy default physics uses default enforcement. check_being_hit() bool Runs hit checks and updates hit-related fields. check_being_grabbed() bool Runs grab checks. check_hitting_entities() bool Runs this character's attack hitboxes against possible victims. A player hits enemies and containers, and other players with friendly damage on. An enemy hits players, and other enemies and containers only with enemies infighting on. check_grab_enforcement() bool Checks grab enforcement rules. try_grab(target, check_vicinity = false, enforcement = true, snap_to_victim = false, allow_airborne = false) bool Attempts to grab another character. target can be a character object or object ID. Airborne targets remain excluded unless explicitly enabled; the script must check its move's height range. For script-owned aerial choreography, use enforcement = false and supply the throw animation/offsets. All other eligibility checks remain in effect. cancel_grab(return_to_standing = true) nil Cancels current grab state. check_pick_up_item() bool Checks item pickup logic. break_held_weapon() bool Breaks the held weapon if its logic names a brokenWeapon : the held item becomes that entity and its breakSound plays. Call it after a hit made with the weapon. False when there is nothing to break. set_weapon(weapon_item_id) nil Assigns a weapon item object ID. A weapon created by the script lasts three drops, as Classic enemies' weapons do, before it vanishes on landing. dispose_weapon() nil Drops or disposes the current weapon through original logic. Throw And Knockdown Methods ¶ Method Returns Detail apply_throw(velocity_x, velocity_y, damage) nil Releases a throw using throw data. velocity_y is converted to fixed-point units; velocity_x is passed as provided by the bridge method. check_thrown_knocking_other_characters() nil Checks thrown-body collision against characters. check_thrown_knocking_items() nil Checks thrown-body collision against containers/items. check_ground_bounce_effect(is_thrown_quake = false) nil Runs ground bounce effect logic. apply_ground_bounce_effect(strength) nil Applies screen/ground bounce strength. on_knockout_move_ended() nil Runs cleanup when a knockout move ends. check_body_breaking_containers() bool Checks body collision against breakable containers with extra width. Movement And Physics Methods ¶ Method Returns Detail set_animation(id, start_frame = 0) nil Inherited from SubItem. Queues a new animation. apply_default_physics() bool Runs local player or enemy default physics depending on the character type. Returns whether the physics step produced a blocking condition such as hit or hit connection. stop_movement() nil Clears movement using the original character controller helper. copy_position_to(other_item_id, offset_x = 0, offset_y = 0) nil Copies this character's item position to another item ID, applying offsets in script units. spawn_explosion(offset_x = 0, offset_y = 0, mode = 10, direction = 3) nil Spawns an explosion effect at an offset. is_pressing_against_walls(include_screen_limits) bool Checks walls and optionally screen limits. is_pressing_against_pits() bool Checks pit borders (grounded pit boundary collision). Use this for the push-wall animation near pit edges. are_in_same_line(other_item_or_id) bool Checks depth/body-line compatibility with another item or item ID. has_events() bool True when the current animation has custom logic events. Killer Mode ¶ The custom game "killer enemies" setting ( hasKillerEnemies ) changes enemy attack animations (animations with hitboxes): their visual frames without a hitbox play for a single update, and an attack that hits a player (not blocking) restarts from frame 0 instead of knocking down. The engine applies this to animations it advances itself, including scripted enemies that only call set_animation . A script that times an attack's frames itself (writing current_animation_frame from its own counters) can honour it with these members: Member Returns Detail is_killer_enemy bool Read. Killer mode applies to this character's attacks (always false for players). killer_skips_frame(animation_id, frame) bool True when killer mode shows the visual frame of attack animation animation_id that contains frame for a single update: killer mode applies, the animation has hitboxes and that visual frame has none. A killer hit rewinds current_animation_frame to 0 during the hit check ( apply_default_physics() or check_hitting_entities() ); a script that sets the frame itself detects the restart by comparing the frame before and after the check: local shown = e.current_animation_frame if e.apply_default_physics() and shown ~= 0 and e.current_animation_frame == 0 and e.is_killer_enemy then my_attack_frame = 0 -- restart the attack in the script's own timing end Score And UI Methods ¶ Method Returns Detail add_score(points, update_visual_score = true) nil Adds score and optionally updates score UI. update_visual_score() nil Refreshes visual score. update_visual_health(other_object_id = -1, update_mutually = true, ignore_other = false) nil Refreshes visual health. update_visual_health_of_other(other_object_id) nil Refreshes another object's visual health. update_visual_lives() nil Refreshes visual lives. distribute_score(score) nil Distributes score to active players. distribute_score_based_on_damage(damage) nil Distributes score using damage as input. check_combo_achievement(increment = 1) nil Checks combo achievement logic. lose_life() bool Runs lose-life logic. Spawn Methods ¶ Method Returns Detail try_spawn_item(...) bool Inherited from Item. Spawns an item or projectile. try_spawn_shuriken(off_x, off_y, vel_x, vel_y, lifetime = 60) bool Spawns a shuriken-style projectile using the original ninja helper. Unlike try_spawn_item , offsets and velocities are passed with the sign used by this helper. Example: Custom Damage Reduction ¶ return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end if character.check_being_hit() then character.damage_taken = character.damage_taken / 2 if character.damage_taken < 1 then character.damage_taken = 1 end end return true end

docs.text: Enemy API ¶ Enemy extends Character with AI state, targeting, movement intent, and enemy-specific counters. It also exposes item and sub-item fields through flattening. Identity And General AI ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail is_alive bool read True when the slot exists and either health or extra health bars ( lives ) remain. Does not require the item/projectile is_active flag. Exact bridge name is IsAlive . is_commoner bool read True when the entity logic marks this as a common enemy. Exact bridge name is IsCommoner . entity_type int read Enemy entity type. Exact bridge name is EntityType ; entity_type from SubItem is also available and writable. character Character read Same object, exposed for interface symmetry. pack_hash int read Pack hash inherited from SubItem. pack_name string read Pack name inherited from SubItem. mode int read/write Current AI/behaviour mode. mode_timer int read/write Frames remaining or elapsed for the current mode, depending on controller. moving_dinrection int read/write Original field name contains the typo Dinrection . Snake-case scripts should use moving_dinrection . distance int read/write Target distance or mode distance parameter. movement_speed int read/write Base movement speed. enemy_status EnemyStatus read/write Overall AI status enum/bitfield. is_boss bool read/write Boss mode. When the last boss in boss mode dies, every other enemy dies with it and its body stays longer before the wave can end. Set it right after spawning a scripted boss. enemy_agressiveness int read/write Aggressiveness value. The bridge and source use the misspelling agressiveness . homing_target_id int read/write Target object ID. Usually a player ID. homing_timer int read/write Retargeting or homing timer. Enemy-Specific Values ¶ These fields mirror original enemy memory slots. They are useful when extending a matching behaviour mode, but they are not general-purpose storage. Prefer custom_value_* for new script state. Property Type Read/Write Detail enemySpecific_C0 int read/write Generic enemy-specific slot. Use exact spelling. abadedeSpecific_C1 int read/write Boss-specific slot. Use exact spelling. abadedeSpecific_C2 int read/write Boss-specific slot. Use exact spelling. enemySpecific_C3 int read/write Generic enemy-specific slot. Use exact spelling. enemySpecific_C4 int read/write Generic enemy-specific slot. Use exact spelling. enemySpecificCounter_C5 int read/write Generic counter slot. Use exact spelling. abadedeSpecific_C6 int read/write Boss-specific slot. Use exact spelling. abadedeSpecific_C7 int read/write Boss-specific slot. Use exact spelling. abadedeSpecificTargetId_C8 int read/write Boss-specific target ID. Use exact spelling. abadedeSpecificCounter_CC int read/write Boss-specific counter. Use exact spelling. shivaSpecific_B0 int read/write Boss-specific slot. Use exact spelling. isBikerRidingBike_CA bool read/write Bike-riding state. Use exact spelling. bikerSpecialCounter_CB int read/write Biker-specific counter. Use exact spelling. biker_next_animation_id int read/write Biker next-animation helper. use_biker_pipe bool read/write Requests biker pipe behaviour. initial_ninja_hook_heigh int read/write Ninja hook height field. Name follows source spelling. AI Override Values ¶ Override fields are writable; probability, timer, speed, and distance fields are read-only values from AI data. The read-only values come from the enemy logic's aiData table: one row per aggressiveness level ( enemy_agressiveness , clamped to the last row), one column per value. The suffix is the original RAM offset; the number after Mode_ is the AI mode the value belongs to. An entity with no AI data reads 0 everywhere. When the native AI picks a random mode it rolls 0..99 and subtracts ProbabilityMode_E0 , then E1 , E2 , E3 and E4 in turn: the first value that takes the roll below zero selects modes 0 to 4, so each is that mode's chance in percent. Writing a non-zero override_aiData_En replaces column n for this enemy only (some native bosses do this at runtime); 0 restores the table value. Property Type Read/Write override_aiData_E0 , override_aiData_E1 , override_aiData_E2 , override_aiData_E3 , override_aiData_E4 int read/write ProbabilityMode_E0 , ProbabilityMode_E1 , ProbabilityMode_E2 , ProbabilityMode_E3 , ProbabilityMode_E4 int read MinTimerMode_0_E6 , RandomTimerMode_0_E7 int read MinTimerMode_1_E8 , RandomTimerMode_1_E9 int read MinSpeedMode_1_EA , RandomSpeedMode_1_EB int read TimerMode_2_EC , MinSpeedMode_2_ED , RandomSpeedMode_2_EE int read MinDistanceMode_3_EF , RandomDistanceMode_3_F0 , MinTimerMode_3_F1 , RandomTimerMode_3_F2 , SpeedMode_3_F3 int read MinTimerMode_4_F4 , RandomTimerMode_4_F5 , MinSpeedMode_4_F6 , RandomSpeedMode_4_F7 int read MinTimerMode_5_F8 , RandomTimerMode_5_F9 , MinSpeedMode_5_FA , RandomSpeedMode_5_FB int read MinTimerMode_6_FC , RandomTimerMode_6_FD int read MinTimerMode_7_FE , RandomTimerMode_7_FF int read Boss AI Read-Only Values ¶ Property Type Read/Write ShivaAI_C0 , ShivaAI_C1 , ShivaAI_C2 , ShivaAI_C3 , ShivaAI_C4 , ShivaAI_C5 , ShivaAI_C6 , ShivaAI_C7 int read AI data columns 0x20 .. 0x27 of the same row, used by Shiva's native controller: C0 , C1 and C2 set the length of his waits (each wait lasts between the value and twice the value, in frames), C3 and C4 are 0..255 thresholds compared against a random byte to choose his next action. C5 .. C7 are read from the table but not used by the native controller, so a custom boss script can use them as its own tuning values. Methods ¶ return_to_standing() ¶ Resets the enemy to its standing state through the original enemy controller helper. return function() local enemy = game.this_enemy if enemy ~= nil and enemy.is_animation_over then enemy.return_to_standing() return false end return true end Enemies also inherit all character, item, and sub-item methods. Example: Retarget And Attack ¶ return function() local enemy = game.this_enemy if enemy == nil then return true end local target = enemy.get_nearest_opponent(true, true, true) if target ~= nil then enemy.homing_target_id = target.object_index enemy.is_facing_right = target.position_x > enemy.position_x if enemy.mode_timer <= 0 then enemy.set_animation(12) enemy.mode_timer = 60 return false end end return true end the inherited ten custom variables. These are signed integer fields in EnemyModel, with no native AI meaning. They participate in snapshot copies and serialization, and reset when an enemy slot is cleared. Coordinate ownership with other scripts.

docs.text: Override fields are writable; probability, timer, speed, and distance fields are read-only values from AI data. The read-only values come from the enemy logic's aiData table: one row per aggressiveness level ( enemy_agressiveness , clamped to the last row), one column per value. The suffix is the original RAM offset; the number after Mode_ is the AI mode the value belongs to. An entity with no AI data reads 0 everywhere. When the native AI picks a random mode it rolls 0..99 and subtracts ProbabilityMode_E0 , then E1 , E2 , E3 and E4 in turn: the first value that takes the roll below zero selects modes 0 to 4, so each is that mode's chance in percent. Writing a non-zero override_aiData_En replaces column n for this enemy only (some native bosses do this at runtime); 0 restores the table value. docs.text: Property Type Read/Write ShivaAI_C0 , ShivaAI_C1 , ShivaAI_C2 , ShivaAI_C3 , ShivaAI_C4 , ShivaAI_C5 , ShivaAI_C6 , ShivaAI_C7 int read AI data columns 0x20 .. 0x27 of the same row, used by Shiva's native controller: C0 , C1 and C2 set the length of his waits (each wait lasts between the value and twice the value, in frames), C3 and C4 are 0..255 thresholds compared against a random byte to choose his next action. C5 .. C7 are read from the table but not used by the native controller, so a custom boss script can use them as its own tuning values.

docs.text: Game API ¶ The game object is the global bridge for Lua scripts. It exposes the current script context, frame state, entity lookup, free-slot lookup, music scheduling, clock control, wave control, and pack hashes. The cinematic acquisition, event state, helper initialization, and selective controller/animation APIs are documented in Script-owned cinematics . Context Properties ¶ Property Type Read/Write Internal source Notes this_character Character read Current player or enemy object ID nil for standalone item scripts. this_player Player read Current player object ID nil unless the script is running for a player. this_enemy Enemy read Current enemy object ID nil unless the script is running for an enemy. this_item Item read Current item object ID Valid for standalone item scripts. Not used for player/enemy scripts because their item state is flattened on this_character . pickup_item Item or nil read Item being collected Set only while an item's pickupScript runs. this_player is the prospective collector. is_current_player bool read Current context ID True for player updates. is_current_enemy bool read Current context ID True for enemy updates. State Properties ¶ Property Type Read/Write Meaning current_frame int read Current frame in the simulation update. global_timer int read Total elapsed game timer. level_id int read Current level ID. scene_id int read Current scene or wave ID. is_in_slow_motion bool read True while slow motion is active. slow_motion_frames_left int read/write Remaining slow-motion frames. Setting this directly is equivalent to changing the game state timer. number_of_active_enemies int read Active enemies, including enemies that may not be alive. number_of_alive_enemies int read Alive enemies according to enemy health/state checks. Enemy count multiplier copies of spawn_scene_enemy spawns are left out, but it is never 0 while one is alive (see stages ). number_of_free_sub_items int read Available sub-item effect slots. Stage control ¶ See Scripted stages for hook timing, units, rollback and visual isolation. API Access Meaning custom_value_1 .. custom_value_16 read/write Signed integers saved in game snapshots; persist across scenes and levels. scripted_camera read/write Bypass automatic camera scrolling while true. camera_x , camera_y read/write Viewport position in pixels, positive right/down. screen_width read Current playable width in pixels. half_playable_extra_width read Half of the extra width widescreen adds on each side of the classic 320-pixel view (40 with widescreen on, 0 with it off), scaled like screen_width for the current level. Add it to classic-layout X positions to keep them centred: screen_width is the classic width plus twice this value. difficulty_index read Zero-based difficulty index. has_instant_spawns read The custom game "instant spawns" setting. Scripted stages pace their own spawns: honour it by dropping spawn delays. has_ninpo_kage_bunshin read The Ninpo Kage Bunshin game mode: each player trails three shadow clones showing where it was 5, 10 and 15 frames ago. A script that runs its own player attacks can attack from those positions too. enemies_multiplier read The custom game enemy count multiplier, 1 to 8. The engine doubles stage spawns itself; a script that runs its own enemies applies it on its own. enemies_velocity_numerator read Numerator of the enemy speed multiplier in effect (the custom game setting, otherwise the difficulty's). Scale a per-tick movement by numerator / denominator . enemies_velocity_denominator read Denominator of the enemy speed multiplier, at least 1. enemy_capacity read Number of enemy slots; first enemy object ID is 4. scene_enemies_cleared read All scene enemy loadcues consumed, spawn delay elapsed, no active enemies. With scriptedEnemies , only active enemies count. spawn_scene_enemy(index) method returning int Spawn one enemies1 cue in a scriptedEnemies scene; enemy object ID or -1. spawn_scene_item(index) method returning int Spawn one items cue in a scriptedItems scene; item/sub-item ID or -1. Camera filtering and automatic cursors are bypassed. change_scene(index) method returning bool Start normal entrance for a zero-based scene in the current level. Return immediately after a successful request. complete_scene() method returning bool Leave the current scene through its sceneExitCodeId exit (walk/fade or stage clear), then enter the next scene normally. False outside active gameplay, so repeated calls cannot restart the transition. Prefer it to advance_wave() / advance_level() when the exit presentation must play; see Scripted stages . For read-only camera-path queries, temporary art presentation, cinematic fades and an existing-actor view mask, see stage presentation . These APIs keep the live gameplay level and wave intact. Lookup Methods ¶ Method Returns Detail get_player(id) Player or nil Returns nil for negative IDs. Throws if a non-negative ID is not a player ID. get_enemy(id) Enemy or nil Returns nil for negative IDs. Throws if a non-negative ID is not an enemy ID. get_character(id) Character or nil Resolves player or enemy IDs. Logs a warning and returns nil for item/sub-item IDs. get_item(id) Item or nil Returns nil for negative IDs. Throws if a non-negative ID is not an item ID. get_sub_item(id) SubItem or nil Returns nil for negative IDs. Throws if a non-negative ID is not a sub-item ID. get_free_enemy(consider_players_count) Enemy or nil Finds the first available enemy slot. The optional argument defaults to true . get_free_item() Item or nil Finds the first available item slot. get_free_sub_item() SubItem or nil Finds the first available sub-item slot. get_entity(id) Player , Enemy , Item , SubItem or nil Resolves any object ID to its actual wrapper; nil for invalid IDs. See Script-owned cinematics . Object IDs are laid out by range: players first, then enemies from ID 4 ( enemy_capacity slots), then items, then sub-items. Property Type Meaning first_item_id int Object ID of the first item slot. IDs below it are characters (players and enemies), so id < game.first_item_id tells a character hit from an item hit (see check_projectile_hit_target() in the Item API ). item_capacity int Number of item slots, starting at first_item_id . first_sub_item_id int Object ID of the first sub-item slot. sub_item_capacity int Number of sub-item (render-only effect) slots, starting at first_sub_item_id . Use get_character for attacker and victim IDs. Use specific lookups only when you know the ID range. Game Control Methods ¶ Method Returns Detail set_clock(seconds) nil Stores the timer as seconds * 100 internally. clock_value int Read-only remaining whole seconds. With scriptedClock , use this with set_clock() to implement a custom countdown. reset_clock() nil Resets the level timer through the game controller. set_slow_motion(frames) nil Sets slow_motion_frames_left . schedule_go_forward_effect() nil Schedules the "GO!" indicator. random(range) int Returns 0..range-1 from the game's deterministic RNG (the same sequence enemy AI uses, so it is replay and netplay safe). range is 2–65535; smaller values return 0. schedule_quake(amplitude_pixels, duration_frames) nil Schedules a fixed-amplitude alternating playfield quake for the current entity. Amplitude is 1–8 pixels and duration is 1–600 display frames; invalid values or a missing entity context are ignored. Schedule any accompanying sound separately. schedule_music(music_name, pack_name) nil Queues background music. If pack_name is omitted or nil , the current game pack is used. is_next_wave_non_scrolling() bool True when the next wave does not require scrolling. get_number_of_active_players() int Counts active player slots. kill_all_enemies(exception_id) nil Defeats all active enemies except the optional object ID. Defaults to no exception. advance_level() nil Advances to the next level. Skips the next level's scene initialisation when called from Lua: use complete_scene() on the last scene, with a stage-clear exit, instead. advance_wave() nil Advances to the next scene/wave. get_potential_score() int Calculates current potential score from game state. update_alternative_palette() nil Reapplies alternative palette rules. get_pack_hash(pack_name) int Returns the runtime hash used by engine data for a pack name. Cinematics and scene flow ¶ These game members are documented with the systems they drive: Members Documented in begin_cinematic(pack_name, script_name, owner_id, max_ticks) , end_cinematic(keep_camera) , is_cinematic , cinematic_tick , cinematic_owner_id Script-owned cinematics get_cinematic_value(index) , set_cinematic_value(index, value) , is_cinematic_actor(id) Script-owned cinematics update_entity_controller(id) , update_entity_animation(id) , schedule_cinematic_quake(amplitude, frames) Script-owned cinematics get_entity(id) , first_item_id , item_capacity , first_sub_item_id , sub_item_capacity Script-owned cinematics and the lookup tables above get_scene_camera_path(level_id, scene_id) , get_previous_presentation(level_id, scene_id) , get_previous_known_presentation(level_id, scene_id) Stage presentation set_cinematic_presentation(level_id, scene_id) , set_cinematic_dark_presentation() , restore_cinematic_presentation() , cinematic_fade , cinematic_hide_existing_entities Stage presentation complete_scene() , change_scene(index) , spawn_scene_enemy(index) , spawn_scene_item(index) , scene_enemies_cleared , scene hooks Scripted stages Example: Safe Wave End ¶ return function() if game.number_of_alive_enemies == 0 then game.schedule_go_forward_effect() game.advance_wave() end return true end Example: Resolve A Stored Target ¶ return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end local target_id = character.custom_value_1 if target_id >= 0 then local target = game.get_character(target_id) if target ~= nil and target.health > 0 then character.is_facing_right = target.position_x > character.position_x end end return true end game.schedule_music_fade(duration_frames) schedules a fade of the currently playing music. The duration uses 60 Hz host frames; zero stops immediately. It uses the normal music effect queue during rollback.

docs.text: Item API ¶ Item represents physical objects in the world: character bodies, weapons, containers, pickups, projectiles, and other interactive objects. It inherits the SubItem API , so animation fields are also available on items. Position And Motion ¶ Most position and motion values are converted by the bridge. The engine stores them multiplied by 1000 ; Lua reads and writes script units. Property Type Read/Write Detail position_x int read/write World X position. position_y int read/write World Y/depth position on the belt-scroller plane. position_offset_x int read/write Extra X offset used by some behaviours. position_offset_y int read/write Height offset from ground. Negative means airborne, 0 means grounded. velocity_x int read/write Per-frame X movement accumulator. velocity_y int read/write Per-frame Y/depth movement accumulator. impulse_x int read/write Horizontal impulse. Default physics adds this to velocity_x . impulse_y int read/write Vertical/height impulse. Default physics adds this to position_offset_y . impulse_z int read/write Depth impulse. Default physics adds this to velocity_y . acceleration_x int read/write Added to impulse_x after movement. acceleration_y int read/write Added to impulse_y after movement. acceleration_z int read/write Added to impulse_z after movement. wall_thrown_flight int read/write A throw's flight state for walls with a maxHeight (rails): 1 thrown but not yet airborne, 3 airborne, 2 landed while still in a thrown mode, 0 otherwise. The engine updates it every frame from the throw modes (0x10/0x12) and height; a body in state 3 is pushed over a rail it comes down on, one in state 1 is put back on the floor side. A script that throws a body itself can set 1 (or 3 when already airborne) to get the same rail behaviour. is_in_the_air bool read Pit-aware air check. True when position_offset_y < 0 , while falling through a pit, or when there is no ground below. unknownPosition4_62_66_X int read/write Original engine position/scratch field. Use exact spelling. unknownPosition4_62_66_Y int read/write Original engine position/scratch field. Use exact spelling. Collision And Body Data ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail collision_box_half_width int read Current body box half-width. Exact bridge name is CollisionBoxHalfWidth . collision_box_height int read Current body box height. collision_box_depth int read Current body box depth. last_hitbox_index int read/write Last hitbox index used for collision checks. Reset when animation changes. hit_pause_timer int read/write Hit pause countdown. Default physics decrements it and exits early. custom_hit_pause_delay_frames int read/write Animation-frame delay after hit pause. The animation updater decrements this before advancing frames. invincibility_timer int read/write Timer used by invincibility logic. Scripted attack policy ¶ override_attack_damage = true uses attack_damage_override (non-negative) for authored character attack boxes. suppress_attack_hits = true suppresses those boxes entirely. Both character and container scans use the policy. It does not change projectile or throw damage. A script must clear the policy when it no longer applies; the value is saved in rollback state and reset on slot reuse. Object Flags ¶ These map to original status bits. Property Type Read/Write Detail is_active bool read/write Item/projectile active flag ( status4 bit 7). Projectiles often clear this when switching to a hit animation. This is not an enemy existence test: normal enemy initialization leaves it clear. Use is_enabled and character health/state when selecting enemies. is_obstacle bool read/write Blocks movement as an obstacle. effect_players_only bool read/write Effect applies only to players. has_weapon bool read/write Character is holding a weapon. weapon Item read Held item if has_weapon and held_item_id are valid. is_being_thrown bool read/write Throw initiation flag. can_land_safely bool read/write Landing can return to a safe state. is_jump_down_attack bool read/write Jump-down attack status. has_double_forward_tap bool read/write Double-forward input status. Useful to clear when consuming dash-style inputs. is_lying_on_the_floor bool read/write Floor/lying status. did_move_ended bool read/write Move-ended status. Name follows the bridge field. is_jump_attack bool read/write Jump attack status. is_blocking bool read/write Blocking status. is_vulnerable bool read/write Can be hit. is_knocked_down bool read/write Knockdown status. is_grabbing bool read/write Currently grabbing another character. is_being_grabbed bool read/write Currently grabbed by another character. is_attacking bool read/write Attack status. is_being_hit bool read/write Hit reaction status. is_hitting_something bool read/write Low-level hit flag. Character also exposes is_hitting_someone . was_hit_from_right bool read/write Direction of the last incoming hit. Weapon, Container, And Timers ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail contained_item_pack_hash int read/write Pack hash for an item contained by a container. contained_item_entity_id int read/write Entity type/id for contained item. held_item_id int read/write Object ID of held item. weapon_health int read/write Remaining durability of a weapon whose logic sets weaponHealth above 0; reading starts it at that configured budget on first use. Writes are clamped to 0 or more; lowering it while a player holds the weapon shows the usage indicator, and the weapon breaks when an attack ends with it at 0. Weapons without a configured weaponHealth do not use it (they keep the classic drop counter). inside_for_two_players_only bool read/write Container/item rule for two-player-only contents. mode_specific_timer int read/write Behaviour-mode timer. grab_combo_count int read/write Grab combo counter. kill_count int read/write Kill counter used by some behaviours. grenadeVelocity_78 int read/write Original grenade-specific velocity field. Use exact spelling. inner_timer int read/write Generic inner timer. Projectiles use this as lifetime. customDamage_28 int read/write Original custom damage field. Use exact spelling. requested_knockdown_attack bool read/write Requests knockdown attack handling. Projectile Fields ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail projectile_damage int read/write Damage for projectile hit checks. projectile_hit_pause int read/write Hit pause applied by projectile hits. projectile_hit_sound_hash int read/write Runtime hash of projectile hit sound; -1 makes the hit silent, 0 uses the entity's projectileHitSoundName . projectile_hit_sound_pack_hash int read/write Runtime hash of sound pack. projectile_hit_sound_channel int read/write Audio channel for projectile hit sound. Methods ¶ check_projectile_hits() ¶ Runs projectile hit detection if is_active is true. Returns true when a hit was detected. Projectile scripts commonly use this result to decide whether to switch to an impact animation. check_projectile_hit_target() ¶ Runs the same active-projectile collision/damage pass as check_projectile_hits() , returning the hit entity ID or -1 for no hit. Character IDs are below game.first_item_id ; container hits return item IDs. Use this instead of the boolean method when a projectile should react differently to characters and containers. Do not call both methods for the same collision pass. is_pressing_against_containers() ¶ Checks collision pressure against containers. has_ground_below() ¶ Pit-aware ground check. Use this for landing checks in custom aerial scripts; when an item is over a pit, the function returns false even if position_offset_y has reached 0 . is_falling_through_pit() ¶ Returns true when the item is in the falling-through-pit state — the item has been marked as currently falling into a pit zone. Use this to detect when a character or item is actively falling into a pit. is_on_pit() ¶ Returns true when the item's position is inside a pit shape region. Unlike is_falling_through_pit , this checks only whether the current position overlaps a pit shape, regardless of fall state. Useful for detecting proximity to pit zones even before falling begins. is_on_treadmill() ¶ Returns true when the item's position is inside a treadmill shape region. Treadmills apply velocity to grounded entities; this method lets scripts detect when the entity is over one. is_on_custom_shape(shape_index) ¶ Returns true when the item's position is inside a custom shape region. Pass 1 for Custom1 shapes or 2 for Custom2 shapes. These shapes have no built-in engine effect and are intended for script-defined gameplay logic. try_spawn_item(pack, name, anim, mode, off_x, off_y, vel_x, vel_y, lifetime = 60, projectile_damage = 0, projectile_hit_pause = 0, hit_sound_name = nil, hit_sound_pack = nil, hit_sound_channel = 0) ¶ Spawns an item or projectile using the caller as the source object. Important internal details: pack is hashed with get_pack_hash . name is hashed as the entity name. anim is converted to the internal doubled animation ID. off_x , off_y , vel_x , and vel_y are converted to fixed-point units. The bridge negates the provided offsets and velocities before passing them to the engine. This matches the original spawn helper's coordinate convention. lifetime initializes projectile lifetime state. The optional projectile hit fields are copied into the spawned item. try_spawn_enemy(pack, entity_id, animation_id, mode, off_x, off_y) ¶ Spawns an enemy by entity ID/type using the caller as the source object. The current implementation passes animation_id directly to the enemy spawn helper, so use the value expected by the target data. update_position_and_check_world_collisions() ¶ Applies position updates and world collision checks through the enemy/world collision helper. Returns true when vertical or horizontal collision occurred. Call this in scripts that return false and own their movement. get_nearest_opponent(in_same_line, forward_check, backward_check) ¶ Returns the nearest opponent character or nil . in_same_line : require compatible depth/body-box line. forward_check : allow targets in front of the object. backward_check : allow targets behind the object. predict_frame_being_hit(frames_into_the_future) ¶ Returns a prediction from the hit scanner for when this item would be hit within the requested future window. Useful for parry, guard, dodge, or counter windows. is_knocked_down_and_near_ground ¶ Read-only bool. True when the object is knocked down and close enough to the ground for landing/ground impact logic. Example: Manual Projectile Loop ¶ return function() local item = game.this_item if item == nil then return true end local should_destroy = item.check_projectile_hits() item.velocity_x = item.velocity_x + item.impulse_x item.velocity_y = item.velocity_y + item.impulse_z item.inner_timer = item.inner_timer - 1 if item.inner_timer <= 0 then should_destroy = true end if item.update_position_and_check_world_collisions() then should_destroy = true end if should_destroy then item.set_animation(48) item.is_active = false end return false end

docs.text: Item represents physical objects in the world: character bodies, weapons, containers, pickups, projectiles, and other interactive objects. It inherits the SubItem API , so animation fields are also available on items.

docs.text: Most position and motion values are converted by the bridge. The engine stores them multiplied by 1000 ; Lua reads and writes script units. Property Type Read/Write Detail position_x int read/write World X position. position_y int read/write World Y/depth position on the belt-scroller plane. position_offset_x int read/write Extra X offset used by some behaviours. position_offset_y int read/write Height offset from ground. Negative means airborne, 0 means grounded. velocity_x int read/write Per-frame X movement accumulator. velocity_y int read/write Per-frame Y/depth movement accumulator. impulse_x int read/write Horizontal impulse. Default physics adds this to velocity_x . impulse_y int read/write Vertical/height impulse. Default physics adds this to position_offset_y . impulse_z int read/write Depth impulse. Default physics adds this to velocity_y . acceleration_x int read/write Added to impulse_x after movement. acceleration_y int read/write Added to impulse_y after movement. acceleration_z int read/write Added to impulse_z after movement. wall_thrown_flight int read/write A throw's flight state for walls with a maxHeight (rails): 1 thrown but not yet airborne, 3 airborne, 2 landed while still in a thrown mode, 0 otherwise. The engine updates it every frame from the throw modes (0x10/0x12) and height; a body in state 3 is pushed over a rail it comes down on, one in state 1 is put back on the floor side. A script that throws a body itself can set 1 (or 3 when already airborne) to get the same rail behaviour. is_in_the_air bool read Pit-aware air check. True when position_offset_y < 0 , while falling through a pit, or when there is no ground below. unknownPosition4_62_66_X int read/write Original engine position/scratch field. Use exact spelling. unknownPosition4_62_66_Y int read/write Original engine position/scratch field. Use exact spelling.

docs.text: Player API ¶ try_special_move() attempts a defensive or offensive special from the current input, using the same height, move availability and health/meter admission checks as native controls. It returns true only when the move starts. Use it for scripted cancels before releasing a victim or resetting state. A successful call also invokes the entity's specialMoveScript once, if present. Player extends Character with human input state and player-specific timers. Because of flattening, a player also exposes character, item, and sub-item fields directly. Identity And State ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail is_alive bool read True when the player is active or can continue. Exact bridge name is IsAlive . player_index int read Player slot/object index. character Character read Same object, exposed for interface symmetry. input_state InputButtons read/write Raw input bitmask. Prefer boolean helpers unless you are deliberately editing raw input. back_attack_pressed bool read/write The back attack button's (X) smooth-controls replay: true on the frames after a press, while back_attack_spam_timer runs. It never reflects the classic controls back attack (attack and jump together); read back_attack_input_pressed for the back attack as the native standing move reads it. is_special_attack_ready bool read True when the player can use special attack logic. is_selecting_game_over bool read/write Game-over selection state. Input Timers ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail special_spam_timer int read/write Special input buffer/spam timer. attack_spam_timer int read/write Attack input buffer/spam timer. jump_spam_timer int read/write Jump input buffer/spam timer. back_attack_spam_timer int read/write Back attack input buffer/spam timer. hold_direction_frames int read/write Frames a direction has been held. extra_delay_after_move int read/write Extra delay state after a move. hold_b_attack_timer int read/write Held attack timer. hold_b_attack_ready bool read/write Held attack ready flag. hold_b_release_timer int read/write Held attack release timer. hold_x_button_consumed bool read/write Tracks whether hold-X input has already been consumed. Held Inputs ¶ Held input properties are true while the button or direction is held. Property Detail is_holding_up Up is held. is_holding_down Down is held. is_holding_left Absolute left is held. is_holding_right Absolute right is held. is_holding_forward Direction the player is facing is held. is_holding_backward Opposite of facing direction is held. is_holding_button_a Special button is held. is_holding_button_b Attack button is held. is_holding_button_c Jump button is held. is_holding_button_x X button is held (back attack). is_holding_button_y Y button is held (pick-up / contextual action). is_holding_button_z Z button is held (super move). forward and backward are computed from is_facing_right . If the player is facing right, forward means right; if facing left, forward means left. Pressed Inputs ¶ Pressed input properties are true only on the frame the input was pressed. Property Detail pressed_up Up was just pressed. pressed_down Down was just pressed. pressed_forward Forward was just pressed relative to facing direction. pressed_backward Backward was just pressed relative to facing direction. pressed_button_a Special was just pressed. pressed_button_b Attack was just pressed. pressed_button_c Jump was just pressed. pressed_button_z Z button was just pressed (super move). pick_up_pressed The pick up input was just pressed, as the native standing move reads it for this player's controls setting: the pick up button (Y) with modern controls, attack with classic (three button) controls. Use it before check_pick_up_item() so a scripted player picks up like the native ones. back_attack_input_pressed The back attack input, as the native standing move reads it for this player's controls setting: the back attack button (X) with modern controls, attack and jump held together with classic (three button) controls. A held input stays true until the move that uses it sets hold_x_button_consumed = true (the native back attack does), and is false again until it is released. Use it, rather than back_attack_pressed , for a scripted standing back attack. held_weapon_input What this frame's inputs ask of the held weapon, as the native standing move reads them: 0 nothing, 1 throw it (attack and jump together, or the back attack with attack or jump held, in classic controls; the pick up button with a direction held; never a melee only weapon), 2 the pick up button alone: pick up an item, or drop the weapon if there is none. 0 without a weapon. Previous Held Input ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail previous_held_buttons HoldInputButtons read/write Previous-frame held input bitmask. previous_held_buttons2 HoldInputButtons read/write Secondary previous held input bitmask. was_previously_holding_left bool read/write Previous-frame left state. was_previously_holding_right bool read/write Previous-frame right state. last_tap_was_right bool read/write Direction of last tap. Air-control scripts often clear previous_held_buttons after applying an initial tap impulse, so the impulse is not applied repeatedly. Methods ¶ has_input_combo(combo_string) ¶ Checks recent input history. Existing logic events use strings like "v>b" ; scripts may also use readable comma-separated sequences where supported by the input-chain parser. if player.has_input_combo("v>b") then player.set_animation(46) return false end check_grab_while_moving() ¶ Runs the original grab-while-moving logic. Use in custom walking or dash states that still need normal grab contact. safe_land() ¶ Returns the player to the safe standing/landing state through knockout move cleanup logic. respawn() ¶ Respawns the player in the current scene. update_position_and_check_world_collisions() ¶ Players override the item implementation and use the player world-collision helper. Returns true when vertical or horizontal collision occurred. Example: Consume A Defensive Input ¶ return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end if player.is_holding_button_x and not player.hold_x_button_consumed then player.hold_x_button_consumed = true player.set_animation(40) return false end return true end Example: Absolute And Relative Direction ¶ return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end -- Absolute direction changes facing. if player.is_holding_left then player.is_facing_right = false elseif player.is_holding_right then player.is_facing_right = true end -- Relative direction starts an attack in front of the player. if player.pressed_forward and player.pressed_button_b then player.set_animation(48) return false end return true end

docs.text: SubItem API ¶ SubItem is the visual and animation layer used by every active object. Players, enemies, characters, and items all inherit these fields through flattening. Free item/subitem slots can be initialized with initialize(pack_name, entity_name, animation_id, mode = 2) . Player/enemy slots and occupied slots are rejected. Helpers created during a cinematic are removed when it ends; see Script-owned cinematics . Identity And Visual State ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail name string read Internal entity name. Exact bridge name is Name . classic_name string read Name of the Classic entity this one behaves as, followed through its logic references: "Pipe" for a mod's bat that references Classic Pipe. nil when it has no Classic base. Use it to tell weapon kinds apart. is_throw_only_weapon bool read The item's own logic.json sets throwOnlyWeapon : a weapon that is only thrown, never swung or stabbed. is_melee_only_weapon bool read The item's own logic.json sets meleeOnlyWeapon : a weapon that is never thrown. is_breakable_weapon bool read The item's own logic.json names a brokenWeapon : it breaks into that entity on its first hit. thrown_damage int read Damage the item deals when it hits as a projectile: its logic projectileDamage , followed through logic references. pack_name string read Content pack name resolved from the pack hash. pack_hash int read Runtime hash for the current pack. Exact bridge name is PackHash . is_enabled bool read True when the slot exists. Exact bridge name is IsEnabled . object_index int read Global object ID for this object. Exact bridge name is ObjectIndex . entity_type int read/write Runtime hash or type ID for the entity. palette_pack int read/write Pack hash for palette lookup. palette_line int read/write Palette row/index. ignore_rendering bool read/write When true, the animation updater does not advance frame progress through the normal rendered path. custom_z_order int read/write Manual render depth in raw engine 16.16 units. Unlike Lua position/screen-position fields, this field does not divide by PositionMultiplier (1000). For a Lua ground coordinate, assign ground * 1000 . Animation And Facing ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail is_facing_right bool read/write Main facing flag. Changes hitbox orientation, forward/backward input interpretation, and spawn direction. direction_signal int read 1 when facing right, -1 when facing left. object_mode int read/write Behaviour mode used by original and reference controllers. For many player standing states, 2 returns to active standing logic. current_animation_id int read/write Editor-facing animation ID. Internally stored doubled. Prefer set_animation for transitions. current_animation_frame int read/write Current animation logic frame. Advanced after movement scripts run. next_animation_id int read/write Queued animation ID. The animation controller copies it into current animation later. next_animation_frame int read/write Start frame used when the animation ID changes, or when the current animation loops. Setting this alone does not seek an animation already playing. is_animation_over bool read/write Read checks whether the current frame has reached the animation duration. Writing true finishes the animation. Writing false has no effect. referenced_object_id int read/write Generic linked object ID used by some behaviours. Screen Position ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail screen_position_x int read/write Screen X in script units. Internally scaled by 1000 . screen_position_y int read/write Screen Y in script units. Internally scaled by 1000 . Generic Script State ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail custom_value_1 through custom_value_10 int read/write Per-object script storage. Use for timers, mode selectors, one-shot flags, and stored object IDs. Read and write these through named properties, such as e.custom_value_1 . Bracket access such as e["custom_value_1"] uses the native entity indexer and does not read that property. For indexed storage helpers, use a table of functions that access the named properties explicitly. Position changes after physics ¶ A scene post-update script runs after character physics has cached screen_position_x/y for rendering. When it makes an instantaneous pose-position change, update those screen coordinates in the same tick as the position/offset and has_just_teleported . Otherwise the new pose is rendered at the previous origin for one frame. For a world-positioned character, use screen_position_x = position_x + position_offset_x and the corresponding Y expression. Internal Buffers ¶ These are exposed because several original behaviours use them. Prefer custom_value_* unless you are matching or extending an original behaviour that already depends on these buffers. Property Type Read/Write Detail customVelocity_DecBuffer_0_4_X int read/write Original decimal/fixed buffer X. Use exact spelling. customVelocity_DecBuffer_0_4_Y int read/write Original decimal/fixed buffer Y. Use exact spelling. customVelocity2_DecBuffer_8_C_X int read/write Secondary original buffer X. Use exact spelling. customVelocity2_DecBuffer_8_C_Y int read/write Secondary original buffer Y. Use exact spelling. customDecBuffer_10 int read/write Original behaviour scratch field. Use exact spelling. customDecBuffer_14 int read/write Original behaviour scratch field. Use exact spelling. customBulletLifetimeDecBuffer_18 int read/write Original projectile lifetime/scratch field. Use exact spelling. has_just_teleported bool read/write Set for an authored instantaneous position/pose change to skip sprite and position smoothing that tick. Also set by the engine for throw anchors and nonzero animation entries. Clears residual grab glide, except on the newly entered grab itself. Grab Offsets ¶ Property Type Read/Write Detail front_grab_offset int read Front grab offset from logic data converted to script units. back_grab_offset int read Back grab offset from logic data converted to script units. held_front_grab_offset int read Distance this entity is held at when grabbed from the front (logic heldFrontGrabOffset ), in script units; 0 when unset (the grabber's front_grab_offset applies). held_back_grab_offset int read Same for a hold from behind (logic heldBackGrabOffset ); 0 when unset (the grabber's back_grab_offset applies). Native grab strikes on an entity held at its own distance are tested as if it stood at the holder's own grab offset, so they reach it. Methods ¶ set_animation(animation_id, start_frame = 0) ¶ Queues an animation change. The argument is the editor-facing ID. Internally the engine stores animation IDs doubled, and the bridge performs that conversion. The change is fully applied by the animation update step. Return false after decisive animation changes if you need to stop the old controller from continuing during the current frame. start_frame is used on an ID transition (and as the loop restart frame), not as an immediate seek of an unchanged animation. An already-playing animation normally increments current_animation_frame later in this same frame. A script-owned pose clock must account for that increment when positioning linked actors. Shared throw controllers also read the thrower's current progress before the animation update: a queued throw ID can otherwise be paired with the old hold's progress. Test delayed throws and the rendered frame after the animation pass, not just the queued ID and start frame. character.set_animation(0) character.object_mode = 2 return false play_sound(pack_name, sound_name, channel_id = 0, pitch_percentage = 100) ¶ Schedules an audio effect on the object's audio index. Only loaded sounds play. Sounds are loaded with the entities that reference them (default sounds, hitbox and sound-event sounds, dependencies.json ); a sound that only a script plays must be listed in the sounds of some loaded entity's dependencies.json , or it stays silent. character.play_sound("My Pack", "guard-impact", 1, 100) show_hit_effect(offset_x, offset_y, big = true, target_id = -1) ¶ Shows the hit sparkle a hitbox contact shows (the big or small Classic spark, drawn in front of every entity), for hits a script applies itself, such as damage written directly to a held actor. offset_x and offset_y are Lua position units from this object: offset_x ahead along its facing, offset_y up. With target_id (an object index) the target also gets the hit vibration a hitbox contact gives it. It only schedules the visual; it does not apply damage or hit pause. -- a knee halfway to the held enemy, 40 px up local ahead = victim.position_x - character.position_x if ahead < 0 then ahead = -ahead end character.show_hit_effect(ahead / 2, 40 * 65536 / 1000, true, victim.object_index) start_palette_fade(frames) ¶ Fades the entity's sprite in from black over frames simulation frames, starting this frame: it is drawn fully dark at the start and at its normal palette when the fade ends. 0 (or a negative value) cancels a fade in progress. The fade start and duration are saved in the entity's state, so it is replay, rollback and netplay safe; the darkening itself is view-only. -- an entity appearing out of the dark over one second entity.start_palette_fade(60) clear_referenced_items() ¶ Clears linked/referenced items through the controller. Use when a move owns spawned helper objects and must clean them up. Example: One-Time Sound ¶ return function() local item = game.this_item if item == nil then return true end if item.custom_value_1 == 0 then item.custom_value_1 = 1 item.play_sound("My Pack", "spawn", 0) end return true end
