docs.text: Combat And Defense Examples ¶ These scripts cover defensive mechanics, weapon-dependent move redirects, break specials, parry windows, and hit-pause reactions. Direction Switch During Attacks ¶ This pattern lets a character face the held direction while attacking, and clears stale victim/attacker links so old hit relationships do not persist after turning around. local function clear_victim_information(character) local victim = character.victim if victim ~= nil then victim.attacker_character_id = -1 end character.attacked_character_id = -1 end return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil or not character.is_player then return true end if character.is_holding_right and not character.is_facing_right then character.is_facing_right = true clear_victim_information(character) elseif character.is_holding_left and character.is_facing_right then character.is_facing_right = false clear_victim_information(character) end return true end Blocking With Hit Absorption ¶ Attach this to a block animation. Throws still beat the block; strikes are absorbed and converted into attacker hit pause. return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end character.is_blocking = true character.is_knocked_down = false -- Grabs are checked before strike absorption so throws can beat blocking. if character.check_being_grabbed() then return true end local was_being_hit = character.is_being_hit character.is_being_hit = false if was_being_hit then local attacker = character.attacker if attacker ~= nil then attacker.hit_pause_timer = attacker.hit_pause_timer + 20 attacker.custom_hit_pause_delay_frames = attacker.custom_hit_pause_delay_frames + 20 character.custom_hit_pause_delay_frames = attacker.custom_hit_pause_delay_frames - 10 end character.is_facing_right = character.was_hit_from_right character.damage_taken = 0 if character.current_animation_frame < 5 then character.current_animation_frame = 5 end end if not character.is_animation_over then return false end character.is_blocking = false character.impulse_x = 0 character.velocity_x = 0 character.inner_timer = 0 character.set_animation(0) character.object_mode = 2 return false end Enter Block From Being Hit ¶ Attach this to a being-hit animation. If the player holds a guard input before the normal hit reaction continues, the script resets to standing so normal back-attack or block checks can run. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local guard_input = player.is_holding_button_x or (player.is_holding_button_b and player.is_holding_button_c) if guard_input and not player.hold_x_button_consumed then player.set_animation(0) player.object_mode = 2 end return true end Predictive Parry ¶ Use predict_frame_being_hit to enter a parry/repel animation only when an incoming hit is close enough. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end if player.custom_value_3 > 0 then player.custom_value_3 = player.custom_value_3 - 1 return true end if not player.pressed_forward then return true end local hit_frame = player.predict_frame_being_hit(14) if hit_frame > 3 then player.set_animation(41) player.has_double_forward_tap = false return false end -- Short cooldown for failed attempts. player.custom_value_3 = 10 return true end Repel On Hit Pause ¶ This aerial counter watches for hit pause. If the attack connects and freezes the move, the script changes into a recoil/repel animation and pushes the character away. return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil or not character.is_player or not character.is_in_the_air then return true end -- Hit pause greater than 1 means the active hit connected recently. if character.hit_pause_timer > 1 then character.set_animation(54) character.impulse_x = -65 * character.direction_signal character.impulse_y = -262 return false end character.impulse_y = character.impulse_y - 13 character.position_offset_y = character.position_offset_y + character.impulse_y character.position_x = character.position_x + character.impulse_x return false end Weapon-Specific Move Redirect ¶ Use this on a blitz or special animation to redirect to a weapon-specific animation when the player holds a specific weapon. For the complete Character Editor workflow, including where to create and attach the script, see Play a Different Animation for a Held Weapon . return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end local weapon = character.weapon if weapon == nil then return true end if weapon.pack_name == "Classic" and weapon.name == "Knife" then character.set_animation(41) return false end return true end Replace 41 with the target animation's editor list position. Entity names and pack names are case-sensitive. Comparing names avoids a magic numeric ID and works for custom weapons as well as original ones. Defensive Break Special ¶ This lets the player spend health to break out with a special. It flips direction if the player is holding the opposite side. local function flip_to_input_direction(character) if character.is_holding_right and not character.is_facing_right then character.impulse_x = -character.impulse_x character.is_facing_right = true elseif character.is_holding_left and character.is_facing_right then character.impulse_x = -character.impulse_x character.is_facing_right = false end end return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end if player.health > 8 and player.pressed_button_a then if player.is_holding_left or player.is_holding_right then flip_to_input_direction(player) player.set_animation(37) player.object_mode = 40 else player.set_animation(35) player.object_mode = 36 end end if player.back_attack_input_pressed then player.hold_x_button_consumed = true flip_to_input_direction(player) player.set_animation(38) player.object_mode = 20 end return true end Aerial Special With Health Cost ¶ This is a full controller replacement: vulnerability window, hit checks, hit pause, custom movement, health cost, and return to standing. local function face_input_direction(character) if character.is_holding_right then character.is_facing_right = true elseif character.is_holding_left then character.is_facing_right = false end end return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end local vulnerable_now = character.current_animation_frame > 33 character.is_vulnerable = vulnerable_now if vulnerable_now and character.check_being_hit() then return false end if character.hit_pause_timer > 0 then character.hit_pause_timer = character.hit_pause_timer - 1 return false end if character.current_animation_frame == 0 then face_input_direction(character) character.impulse_x = 300 character.impulse_y = 200 character.is_jump_down_attack = false character.is_jump_attack = false elseif character.current_animation_frame == 24 then face_input_direction(character) character.impulse_x = 400 end if character.is_animation_over then character.health = character.health - 8 character.acceleration_x = 0 character.acceleration_y = 0 character.acceleration_z = 0 character.impulse_x = 0 character.impulse_y = 0 character.impulse_z = 0 character.is_vulnerable = true character.set_animation(0) character.object_mode = 2 return false end if not character.is_in_the_air and character.impulse_x > 0 then local ground_acceleration_x = -20 if character.current_animation_frame > 24 then ground_acceleration_x = -30 end character.impulse_x = character.impulse_x + ground_acceleration_x if character.impulse_x < 0 then character.impulse_x = 0 end end character.check_hitting_entities() character.velocity_x = character.velocity_x + character.impulse_x * character.direction_signal if character.position_offset_y < 0 then character.velocity_y = character.velocity_y + character.impulse_z character.position_offset_y = character.position_offset_y + character.impulse_y character.impulse_y = character.impulse_y + 32 if character.position_offset_y >= 0 then character.position_offset_y = 0 end end return false end

It flips direction if the player is holding the opposite side. local function flip_to_input_direction(character) if character.is_holding_right and not character.is_facing_right then character.impulse_x = -character.impulse_x character.is_facing_right = true elseif character.is_holding_left and character.is_facing_right then character.impulse_x = -character.impulse_x character.is_facing_right = false end end return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end if player.health > 8 and player.pressed_button_a then if player.is_holding_left or player.is_holding_right then flip_to_input_direction(player) player.set_animation(37) player.object_mode = 40 else player.set_animation(35) player.object_mode = 36 end end if player.back_attack_input_pressed then player.hold_x_button_consumed = true flip_to_input_direction(player) player.set_animation(38) player.object_mode = 20 end return true end

docs.text: This is a full controller replacement: vulnerability window, hit checks, hit pause, custom movement, health cost, and return to standing. local function face_input_direction(character) if character.is_holding_right then character.is_facing_right = true elseif character.is_holding_left then character.is_facing_right = false end end return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end local vulnerable_now = character.current_animation_frame > 33 character.is_vulnerable = vulnerable_now if vulnerable_now and character.check_being_hit() then return false end if character.hit_pause_timer > 0 then character.hit_pause_timer = character.hit_pause_timer - 1 return false end if character.current_animation_frame == 0 then face_input_direction(character) character.impulse_x = 300 character.impulse_y = 200 character.is_jump_down_attack = false character.is_jump_attack = false elseif character.current_animation_frame == 24 then face_input_direction(character) character.impulse_x = 400 end if character.is_animation_over then character.health = character.health - 8 character.acceleration_x = 0 character.acceleration_y = 0 character.acceleration_z = 0 character.impulse_x = 0 character.impulse_y = 0 character.impulse_z = 0 character.is_vulnerable = true character.set_animation(0) character.object_mode = 2 return false end if not character.is_in_the_air and character.impulse_x > 0 then local ground_acceleration_x = -20 if character.current_animation_frame > 24 then ground_acceleration_x = -30 end character.impulse_x = character.impulse_x + ground_acceleration_x if character.impulse_x < 0 then character.impulse_x = 0 end end character.check_hitting_entities() character.velocity_x = character.velocity_x + character.impulse_x * character.direction_signal if character.position_offset_y < 0 then character.velocity_y = character.velocity_y + character.impulse_z character.position_offset_y = character.position_offset_y + character.impulse_y character.impulse_y = character.impulse_y + 32 if character.position_offset_y >= 0 then character.position_offset_y = 0 end end return false end

docs.text: Enemy AI Examples ¶ Enemy scripts can be attached once to the entity in logic.json , so the same AI runs regardless of which animation or state the enemy is currently in: "aiScript": { "packName": "My Chronicle", "scriptName": "My Enemy AI" } The file lives at Editor/<Pack Name>/Scripts/My Enemy AI.lua . The script's update function runs once per frame before the enemy's native controller and receives the normal game global; the current enemy is available as game.this_enemy . This setting belongs to the enemy entity. When a custom level spawns that entity, its instances automatically use the declared AI; level spawn data does not need a script field. aiScript is not inherited from referenceEntityName , so put it in the custom entity's own logic.json when the custom entity should use it. Return false when the script handled the frame. The native enemy controller is skipped. Return true to let the native controller continue, which lets a script augment existing AI. Animation scripts remain useful for behavior belonging to one particular move. Use aiScript for decisions that must follow the enemy across standing, walking, wind-up, and attack states. Complete Entity-Level Example ¶ The following can be used as the entity's aiScript . It handles hook-drop setup, hit interruptions, facing, delay before action, distance gating, and grounded versus aerial attack selection. Because it runs in every state, it first leaves non-standing animations to their normal controller. local distance_to_attack = 12000 return function() local enemy = game.this_enemy if enemy == nil then return true end -- Restrict this decision block to the entity's standing state. Replace 0 with the -- appropriate mode if this enemy uses a different standing mode. if enemy.object_mode ~= 0 then return true end if enemy.check_being_hit() then -- The hit check already changed state. Stop standing AI for this frame. return false end if enemy.initial_ninja_hook_heigh ~= 0 then -- Some spawn paths put this enemy on a ceiling hook. Convert that setup -- value into real height once, then clear it so it is not applied again. enemy.position_offset_y = -enemy.initial_ninja_hook_heigh enemy.initial_ninja_hook_heigh = 0 end -- Arguments are: -- in_same_line: false means any depth line is allowed. -- forward_check: true allows targets in front. -- backward_check: true allows targets behind. local target = enemy.get_nearest_opponent(false, true, true) if target == nil then return true end enemy.is_facing_right = target.position_x > enemy.position_x -- Wait before attacking. This gives the spawn or idle animation time to read. if enemy.current_animation_frame < 120 then return true end local distance = enemy.position_x - target.position_x if distance < -distance_to_attack then -- Too far to the left of the target: return to roaming behaviour. enemy.object_mode = 0 end if distance < 0 then distance = -distance end if distance < distance_to_attack then if enemy.position_offset_y == 0 then enemy.set_animation(1) else enemy.set_animation(2) enemy.impulse_y = -250 end return false end return true end Same-Line Melee Gate ¶ Use this for enemies that should only attack when they are aligned on the belt-scroller depth axis. return function() local enemy = game.this_enemy if enemy == nil then return true end if enemy.check_being_hit() then return false end local target = enemy.get_nearest_opponent(true, true, true) if target == nil then return true end enemy.is_facing_right = target.position_x > enemy.position_x local dx = enemy.position_x - target.position_x if dx < 0 then dx = -dx end if dx < 5000 then enemy.set_animation(3) return false end return true end Retreat, Then Attack ¶ This pattern uses a custom value as an AI phase. Phase 0 retreats from the nearest target; phase 1 turns around and attacks. return function() local enemy = game.this_enemy if enemy == nil then return true end if enemy.check_being_hit() then enemy.custom_value_1 = 0 return false end local target = enemy.get_nearest_opponent(false, true, true) if target == nil then return true end if enemy.custom_value_1 == 0 then enemy.is_facing_right = target.position_x < enemy.position_x enemy.velocity_x = 120 * enemy.direction_signal enemy.custom_value_2 = enemy.custom_value_2 + 1 if enemy.custom_value_2 > 35 then enemy.custom_value_1 = 1 enemy.custom_value_2 = 0 end return false end enemy.is_facing_right = target.position_x > enemy.position_x enemy.set_animation(4) enemy.custom_value_1 = 0 return false end Enemy Projectile Volley ¶ This example fires a three-shot spread from an enemy attack animation. It uses try_spawn_item because the enemy chooses the volley dynamically. -- Each row is projectile animation id, velocity X, velocity Y/depth. Built once. local shots = { {0, 420, -80}, {0, 480, 0}, {0, 420, 80} } return function() local enemy = game.this_enemy if enemy == nil then return true end if enemy.check_being_hit() then return false end if enemy.current_animation_frame == 10 then for i = 1, #shots do local shot = shots[i] enemy.try_spawn_item( "My Pack", "Enemy Projectile", shot[1], -1, -900, 0, shot[2], shot[3], 80, 6, 3, "projectile-hit", "My Pack", 0 ) end end if enemy.is_animation_over then enemy.set_animation(0) return false end return true end Falling Ambush ¶ Use this when an enemy starts above the ground and should attack after dropping. return function() local enemy = game.this_enemy if enemy == nil then return true end if enemy.check_being_hit() then return false end if enemy.current_animation_frame == 0 and enemy.position_offset_y == 0 then -- Start above the floor. Negative height means airborne. enemy.position_offset_y = -4000 enemy.impulse_y = 0 end enemy.position_offset_y = enemy.position_offset_y + enemy.impulse_y enemy.impulse_y = enemy.impulse_y + 24 if enemy.position_offset_y >= 0 then enemy.position_offset_y = 0 enemy.impulse_y = 0 enemy.set_animation(5) return false end return false end AI Authoring Notes ¶ Put cross-state decisions in the entity-level aiScript ; keep the mechanics of one move in that animation's script. get_nearest_opponent(true, true, true) is good for melee because it requires depth-line compatibility. get_nearest_opponent(false, true, true) is good for facing or projectile decisions. Always call check_being_hit() in custom enemy controllers that return false . If the script changes to a new animation, return false so the old AI does not continue acting for the same frame. Store AI phase and cooldowns in custom_value_* . Locals inside the update function start over on every call, and locals outside it are shared by every enemy using the script.

docs.text: Global Update Hook Examples ¶ Pack-level hooks run around every active entity update. They are powerful because they can change universal combat rules, but they are also expensive and easy to over-apply. Keep them small, guard by context, and return quickly for entities that do not need the rule. Configure Global Hooks ¶ Add hooks to config.json with the same script shape used by animation scripts: { "preEntityUpdateScripts": [ { "packName": "My Pack", "scriptName": "Global entities pre-update" } ], "postEntityUpdateScripts": [ { "packName": "My Pack", "scriptName": "Global entities post-update" } ] } Pre-entity hooks run before the entity controller. Returning false from a pre hook cancels that entity update for the frame. Post-entity hooks run after the entity controller and are best for cleanup or reactions to what just happened. Pre-Update: Thrown Bodies Break Containers ¶ Use a pre hook when you need to adjust vulnerability before normal collision and physics run. return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end -- Object mode 10 and 6 are the example knocked/thrown modes. -- Use the modes that mean airborne damage state in your data. if character.object_mode == 10 or character.object_mode == 6 then -- Prevent normal hits from interrupting this thrown-body rule before the -- post hook decides whether the body can be juggled. character.is_vulnerable = false if character.check_body_breaking_containers() then -- If the body breaks a container, bounce it away. is_being_thrown -- identifies active throw releases; those already own X velocity. if not character.is_being_thrown then character.velocity_x = -character.velocity_x / 3 end character.auxiliar_velocity_x = -character.auxiliar_velocity_x / 3 character.impulse_y = -120 end end return true end Post-Update: Juggle And Multi-Hit Limiter ¶ This post hook creates a global juggle rule. It lets knocked-down characters be hit in the air, applies diminishing damage, changes the hit reaction, and stops the rule after a limit. return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end -- Let hit pause finish. During hit pause, the entity should not be re-tested -- for another global juggle hit every frame. if character.hit_pause_timer ~= 0 then return true end local juggle_limit = 15 local divider_limit = 8 local increment = 1 if character.is_player then -- Players reach the limit faster than enemies in this example. increment = 3 end if character.object_mode == 10 or character.object_mode == 6 then if character.is_pressing_against_walls(true) then character.is_facing_right = not character.is_facing_right if not character.is_being_thrown then character.velocity_x = -character.velocity_x / 2 end character.auxiliar_velocity_x = (character.auxiliar_velocity_x * 3) / 4 character.impulse_y = character.impulse_y - 10 character.hit_pause_timer = 6 end -- current_animation_id 12 is treated as non-juggleable in this example. character.is_vulnerable = character.current_animation_id ~= 12 and character.custom_value_5 < juggle_limit if not character.is_vulnerable then character.is_knocked_down = false return true end character.is_knocked_down = true -- Later hits do less damage. Guard the first two hits so division does not -- over-reduce the opening juggle hits. if character.custom_value_5 > 1 then character.damage_taken = character.damage_taken / character.custom_value_5 end if character.check_being_hit() then character.set_animation(10) character.custom_value_5 = character.custom_value_5 + increment if character.custom_value_5 < divider_limit then character.impulse_y = character.impulse_y / character.custom_value_5 else -- After the divider limit, force the body downward so the juggle -- naturally ends. character.impulse_y = (character.custom_value_5 - divider_limit) * 20 end end else -- Reset the per-character juggle counter outside knocked/thrown modes. character.custom_value_5 = 0 end return true end Post-Update: Air Recovery Escape ¶ This hook lets players recover out of a knockdown on the first airborne hit-reaction frame by holding up plus jump. return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil or not character.is_player then return true end local can_air_recover = character.object_mode == 10 and character.current_animation_id == 11 and character.current_animation_frame == 0 and character.is_holding_up and character.is_holding_button_c if can_air_recover then -- Clear the global juggle counter and mark the character as recovered. character.custom_value_5 = 0 character.is_knocked_down = false -- safe_land returns the player to a valid grounded state if the engine -- considers the character close enough to land safely. character.safe_land() end return true end Global Hit Aura With Per-Target Cooldown ¶ Use a post hook for effects that should damage targets near a special owner or spawned field. The example below assumes another script sets custom_value_7 on characters inside the aura. return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil or not character.is_enemy then return true end -- custom_value_8 is this target's local cooldown. Without it, a global aura -- would hit every frame and drain health instantly. if character.custom_value_8 > 0 then character.custom_value_8 = character.custom_value_8 - 1 return true end if character.custom_value_7 == 1 then character.damage_taken = 2 character.is_being_hit = true -- check_being_hit applies the normal hit reaction fields and links. character.check_being_hit() character.custom_value_8 = 12 end return true end Hook Performance Checklist ¶ Guard with game.this_character , game.this_player , game.this_enemy , or game.this_item immediately. Use object modes and animation IDs to avoid running logic on unrelated states. Prefer custom_value_* cooldowns over scanning every entity every frame. Avoid require inside hot hook bodies unless you intentionally load shared helper modules once. Keep projectiles and effects in animation scripts when the rule only affects that one move.

docs.text: Grabs And Throws Examples ¶ Grab scripts are state machines shared by two characters: the attacker and the victim. The attacker usually owns the script, but the script must keep the victim aligned, vulnerable or invulnerable, animated, and released at the correct time. The examples below use neutral animation IDs and behaviour modes. Replace them with the IDs used by your character logic. Important Grab Rules ¶ character.victim resolves attacked_character_id . It becomes nil if no valid victim is connected. front_grab_offset is read from the attacker's logic data. It is the stable anchor for holding the victim in front of the attacker. position_offset_y controls height. A grabbed airborne victim usually has a negative offset. mode_specific_timer is used by several original grab behaviours as a release timer. Holding it high prevents unwanted automatic release. try_grab(target, check_vicinity, enforcement, snap_to_victim) is useful when a script needs to convert a hit or branch back into a grab. cancel_grab() clears the grab relationship before a throw release or recovery. Force A Back Grab Into A Front Grab ¶ Attach this to a back-grab hold or back-grab transition. When the animation ends, it turns the victim around and enters the normal front-grab hold. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end player.is_vulnerable = true if player.is_animation_over and player.victim ~= nil then -- Face the victim toward the attacker. Front-grab logic expects this. player.victim.is_facing_right = not player.is_facing_right -- Animation 4 is the example front-grab hold. -- Object mode 26 is the example front-grab behaviour mode. player.set_animation(4) player.object_mode = 26 -- We made a decisive state change. Stop the previous grab controller. return false end return true end Grab Hit Repositioning ¶ Use this when a grab attack has an impact section and then returns to a hold. The victim offset changes during the hit frames, then snaps back to the carry offset. local grabbed_offset_x = 1040 local grabbed_offset_y = -1800 local hit_offset_x = 100 local hit_offset_y = -1500 return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end player.is_vulnerable = true player.object_mode = 22 local victim = player.victim if victim == nil then return true end victim.is_vulnerable = true if player.is_animation_over then -- Return to the hold animation at the frame where the victim is already -- aligned. This avoids replaying the initial snap frames. player.set_animation(4, 9) end if player.current_animation_frame < 6 then victim.position_offset_y = hit_offset_y victim.position_offset_x = hit_offset_x else victim.position_offset_y = grabbed_offset_y victim.position_offset_x = grabbed_offset_x end if not player.is_facing_right then victim.position_offset_x = -victim.position_offset_x end return true end Walk While Holding A Victim ¶ This is the core grab-hold controller: keep the victim attached, let the attacker walk, and branch into throws or jumps. local grabbed_offset_x = 1040 local grabbed_offset_y = -1800 local grab_walk_speed_x = 80 local grab_walk_speed_y = 50 local prepare_jump_offset_x = 800 local prepare_jump_offset_y = -1000 local function get_extra_bob_offset(player) local frame = player.current_animation_frame % 35 -- Small vertical offsets make the victim follow the walk cycle. -- The values are in script units, not sprite pixels. if frame < 3 then return 4 elseif (frame >= 3 and frame < 6) or frame >= 33 then return 3 elseif (frame >= 6 and frame < 9) or (frame >= 18 and frame < 27) or frame >= 30 then return 2 end return 0 end return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end player.object_mode = 26 player.is_vulnerable = true local victim = player.victim if victim == nil then return true end victim.is_vulnerable = true -- Hold the original release timer high so this script decides when the grab -- ends. Without this, inherited grab logic can release the victim early. player.mode_specific_timer = 99 if player.pressed_button_b then if player.is_holding_backward or player.is_holding_forward then -- Direction plus attack starts the example slam. victim.is_facing_right = player.is_facing_right player.set_animation(5) player.object_mode = 28 return false elseif victim.is_in_the_air then -- While the victim is airborne, choose one of two follow-up strikes. if player.grab_combo_count < 4 then player.set_animation(33) else player.set_animation(34) end return false end elseif victim.is_in_the_air then if player.pressed_button_c then -- Jump while carrying the victim. The victim is pre-positioned before -- the jump animation starts so the first airborne frame is stable. player.set_animation(3) player.impulse_x = 0 victim.position_offset_y = prepare_jump_offset_y victim.position_offset_x = prepare_jump_offset_x if not player.is_facing_right then victim.position_offset_x = -victim.position_offset_x end return false elseif player.is_holding_backward then -- Rewind the hold cycle for a backward tug. player.set_animation(44) player.current_animation_frame = player.current_animation_frame - 2 if player.current_animation_frame < 0 then player.current_animation_frame = 34 player.has_just_teleported = true end elseif player.is_holding_forward or player.is_holding_up or player.is_holding_down then player.set_animation(44) else player.set_animation(4, 9) end end if player.current_animation_id == 4 then if player.current_animation_frame < 9 and victim.is_in_the_air then -- Skip startup frames when re-entering the hold from an airborne branch. player.current_animation_frame = 9 player.has_just_teleported = true elseif player.current_animation_frame >= 9 then victim.position_offset_y = grabbed_offset_y victim.position_offset_x = grabbed_offset_x if not player.is_facing_right then victim.position_offset_x = -victim.position_offset_x end end elseif player.current_animation_id == 44 then if player.current_animation_frame == 4 then player.impulse_y = vertical_impulse end player.position_offset_y = player.position_offset_y + player.impulse_y player.impulse_y = player.impulse_y + 16 player.velocity_x = player.impulse_x local victim = player.victim if player.impulse_y > 0 and player.position_offset_y >= 0 then -- Land back into the hold and prepare the victim for the next branch. player.set_animation(47) player.impulse_y = 0 player.position_offset_y = 0 if victim ~= nil then victim.position_offset_y = prepare_jump_offset_y victim.position_offset_x = prepare_jump_offset_x if not player.is_facing_right then victim.position_offset_x = -victim.position_offset_x end end return false end if victim == nil then return false end victim.is_vulnerable = true victim.position_offset_x = grabbed_offset_x local grab_offset = player.front_grab_offset if not player.is_facing_right then victim.position_offset_x = -victim.position_offset_x grab_offset = -grab_offset end victim.position_x = player.position_x + grab_offset victim.position_y = player.position_y + 1 + player.velocity_y victim.position_offset_y = player.position_offset_y + It disables victim vulnerability while carried, applies throw damage on impact, cancels the grab, and puts the attacker into a rebound animation. local ground_level = 1000 local function get_victim_offset(player) local frame = player.current_animation_frame if frame < 4 then return -150, -1800 elseif frame < 10 then return -500, -1300 end return -1100, -1000 end return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end player.position_offset_y = player.position_offset_y + player.impulse_y player.impulse_y = player.impulse_y + 16 player.velocity_x = player.impulse_x if player.current_animation_id == 50 then -- Rebound/recovery animation after impact. if player.impulse_y > 0 and player.position_offset_y >= 0 then player.impulse_x = 0 player.impulse_y = 0 player.position_offset_y = 0 player.object_mode = 2 player.is_vulnerable = true player.set_animation(15) end return false end player.is_vulnerable = false if player.current_animation_frame == 0 then player.play_sound("My Pack", "throw-start", 2) end local victim = player.victim if player.impulse_y > 0 and player.position_offset_y >= ground_level then victim_was_dying = victim.object_mode == 6 -- apply_throw releases the victim with throw damage and vertical force. victim.apply_throw(-2, -220, 0) victim.is_being_thrown = false victim.is_facing_right = player.is_facing_right victim.set_animation(18) victim.damage_taken = 56 if victim.current_animation_frame < 16 then victim.current_animation_frame = 16 end local offset_x, offset_y = get_victim_offset(player) victim.position_offset_x = offset_x local grab_offset = player.front_grab_offset if not player.is_facing_right then victim.position_offset_x = -victim.position_offset_x grab_offset = -grab_offset end victim.position_x = player.position_x + grab_offset victim.position_y = player.position_y + 1 + player.velocity_y victim.position_offset_y = The script keeps the victim above the ground and lets their default physics apply the new impulse. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local victim = player.victim if victim ~= nil and victim.impulse_y > -300 then victim.impulse_y = -300 -- Apply the victim's normal physics immediately so the new impulse takes -- effect during this frame instead of waiting for their next update. victim.apply_default_physics() return false end if player.current_animation_frame == 0 and player.is_holding_down and victim ~= nil and player.try_grab(victim) then -- Convert the combo end back into a throw if down is held. victim.is_facing_right = player.is_facing_right player.set_animation(5) player.object_mode = 28 return false end player.combo_count = 0 player.extra_delay_after_move = 8 return true end

docs.text: Grab scripts are state machines shared by two characters: the attacker and the victim. The attacker usually owns the script, but the script must keep the victim aligned, vulnerable or invulnerable, animated, and released at the correct time. The examples below use neutral animation IDs and behaviour modes. Replace them with the IDs used by your character logic.
docs.title: Grabs And Throws Examples

docs.text: character.victim resolves attacked_character_id . It becomes nil if no valid victim is connected. front_grab_offset is read from the attacker's logic data. It is the stable anchor for holding the victim in front of the attacker. position_offset_y controls height. A grabbed airborne victim usually has a negative offset. mode_specific_timer is used by several original grab behaviours as a release timer. Holding it high prevents unwanted automatic release. try_grab(target, check_vicinity, enforcement, snap_to_victim) is useful when a script needs to convert a hit or branch back into a grab. cancel_grab() clears the grab relationship before a throw release or recovery.

Stop the previous grab controller. return false end return true end

docs.text: Movement And Input Examples ¶ These scripts cover player-owned movement: air steering, jump height, wall jumps, speed tiers, rolling momentum, and charge release. They are adapted from several Test chronicle prototypes and cleaned up into reusable patterns. Simple Air Steering ¶ Attach this to a jump or aerial attack when you want the original controller to keep handling landing and collisions. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end -- Absolute left/right input is used for air steering because the player -- expects left to move left even if the character is facing right. local max_air_speed = 130 local acceleration = 7 if player.is_in_the_air then if player.is_holding_right and player.impulse_x < max_air_speed then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x + acceleration -- The previous-frame flag identifies the first held frame after a tap. -- Snap to the starting speed once, then clear the old input state so -- the snap is not applied again next frame. if player.was_previously_holding_right then player.impulse_x = max_air_speed player.previous_held_buttons = 0 end elseif player.is_holding_left and player.impulse_x > -max_air_speed then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x - acceleration if player.was_previously_holding_left then player.impulse_x = -max_air_speed player.previous_held_buttons = 0 end end end -- Only steering was changed. Let the jump controller keep running. return true end Walk And Run Air-Control Profiles ¶ Use tiny setup scripts on different jump-start animations, then share one air-control script across all aerial states. Walk-jump setup: return function() local player = game.this_player if player ~= nil then -- Profile 1 means normal walk-jump steering. player.custom_value_1 = 1 end return true end Run-jump setup: return function() local player = game.this_player if player ~= nil then -- Profile 2 means faster run-jump steering. player.custom_value_1 = 2 end return true end Shared aerial script: return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local initial_velocity = 50 local max_velocity = 110 local acceleration = 16 if player.custom_value_1 == 2 then initial_velocity = 100 max_velocity = 190 acceleration = 20 end if player.is_in_the_air then if player.is_holding_right and player.impulse_x < max_velocity then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x + acceleration if player.was_previously_holding_right then player.impulse_x = initial_velocity player.previous_held_buttons = 0 end elseif player.is_holding_left and player.impulse_x > -max_velocity then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x - acceleration if player.was_previously_holding_left then player.impulse_x = -initial_velocity player.previous_held_buttons = 0 end end else -- Grounded direction changes update facing and reset to normal profile. if player.is_holding_right and not player.is_facing_right then player.is_facing_right = true player.custom_value_1 = 1 elseif player.is_holding_left and player.is_facing_right then player.is_facing_right = false player.custom_value_1 = 1 end end return true end Variable Jump Height ¶ This script shortens upward momentum when the player releases jump early. It can be layered into an existing jump script that still returns true . return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local small_jump_force = 262 -- Negative impulse_y means the character is rising. -- If the jump button is no longer held, clamp upward speed. if player.impulse_y < -small_jump_force and not player.is_holding_button_c then player.impulse_y = -small_jump_force end return true end Full Manual Air Physics ¶ Use this when an aerial attack owns movement and landing. It handles hits, gravity, horizontal steering, wall stopping, and landing. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local gravity = 14 local air_acceleration = 6 local top_speed = 393 -- Since this script replaces the controller, it must check interruptions. if player.check_being_hit() then return false end -- Let active hitboxes connect. If the move hits something, rebound both -- horizontal and vertical impulses to produce a bounce-like feel. if player.check_hitting_entities() then player.impulse_x = -player.impulse_x player.impulse_y = -player.impulse_y end player.impulse_y = player.impulse_y + gravity if player.is_holding_left then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x - air_acceleration elseif player.is_holding_right then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x + air_acceleration end if player.impulse_x > top_speed then player.impulse_x = top_speed elseif player.impulse_x < -top_speed then player.impulse_x = -top_speed end player.velocity_x = player.impulse_x player.position_offset_y = player.position_offset_y + player.impulse_y if player.is_pressing_against_walls(true) then player.impulse_x = 0 end if player.impulse_y > 0 and player.position_offset_y >= 0 then player.impulse_y = 0 player.position_offset_y = 0 player.set_animation(0) player.object_mode = 2 end return false end Wall Jump ¶ This script freezes briefly on the wall, flips facing once, then lets the player launch away. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local wall_freeze_frames = 8 if player.current_animation_frame < wall_freeze_frames then if player.current_animation_frame == 0 then -- Flip once at the start so forward now points away from the wall. player.is_facing_right = not player.is_facing_right end -- Stop the normal controller while the character clings to the wall. return false end local away_speed = 131 if player.is_holding_forward then away_speed = 196 elseif player.is_holding_backward then away_speed = 65 end player.velocity_x = away_speed * player.direction_signal player.impulse_y = player.impulse_y + 13 player.position_offset_y = player.position_offset_y + player.impulse_y if player.pressed_button_c and player.is_pressing_against_walls(true) then player.set_animation(56) player.impulse_y = -307 player.play_sound("My Pack", "wall-jump", 2) end return false end Rolling Momentum Controller ¶ This is a fuller player controller: acceleration, deceleration, depth movement, wall checks, jump, pickup, roll transition, and animation speed control. local acceleration_x = 3 local deceleration_x = 32 local friction_x = 3 local top_speed_x = 393 local acceleration_z = 1 local deceleration_z = 17 local friction_z = 1 local top_speed_z = 196 local breaking_speed = 262 local rolling_minimum_speed = 32 local jump_force = 426 local function abs(value) if value < 0 then return -value end return value end local function stop_all_motion(player) player.velocity_x = 0 player.velocity_y = 0 player.impulse_x = 0 player.impulse_z = 0 end return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end if player.check_being_hit_or_grabbed() then return false end local is_breaking = false if player.is_holding_left then if player.impulse_x > 0 then is_breaking = true player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x - deceleration_x if player.impulse_x < 0 then player.impulse_x = 0 end elseif player.impulse_x > -top_speed_x then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x - acceleration_x end elseif player.is_holding_right then if player.impulse_x < 0 then is_breaking = true player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x + deceleration_x if player.impulse_x > 0 then player.impulse_x = 0 end elseif player.impulse_x < top_speed_x then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x + acceleration_x end else if player.impulse_x > 0 then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x - friction_x if player.impulse_x < 0 then player.impulse_x = 0 end elseif player.impulse_x < 0 then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x + friction_x if player.impulse_x > 0 then player.impulse_x = 0 end end end if player.impulse_x > top_speed_x then player.impulse_x = top_speed_x elseif player.impulse_x < -top_speed_x then player.impulse_x = -top_speed_x end -- Depth movement uses impulse_z and velocity_y. if player.is_holding_up then player.impulse_z = player.impulse_z - acceleration_z elseif player.is_holding_down then player.impulse_z = player.impulse_z + acceleration_z else if player.impulse_z > 0 then player.impulse_z = player.impulse_z - friction_z if player.impulse_z < 0 then player.impulse_z = 0 end elseif player.impulse_z < 0 then player.impulse_z = player.impulse_z + friction_z if player.impulse_z > 0 then player.impulse_z = 0 end end end if player.impulse_z > top_speed_z then player.impulse_z = top_speed_z elseif player.impulse_z < -top_speed_z then player.impulse_z = -top_speed_z end player.velocity_x = player.impulse_x player.velocity_y = player.impulse_z local total_speed = abs(player.impulse_x) + abs(player.impulse_z) if player.is_pressing_against_walls(true) then if player.is_holding_left or player.is_holding_right then player.set_animation(44) else player.impulse_x = 0 end total_speed = 0 end if player.pressed_button_b and total_speed < rolling_minimum_speed and player.check_pick_up_item() then player.set_animation(14) player.object_mode = 44 stop_all_motion(player) return false end if player.pressed_button_c or player.pressed_button_a then player.set_animation(2) player.impulse_y = -jump_force player.play_sound("My Pack", "jump", 2) return false end if player.is_holding_button_b then if total_speed < rolling_minimum_speed then player.set_animation(46) stop_all_motion(player) else player.set_animation(48) player.play_sound("My Pack", "roll", 2) end return false end if player.impulse_x ~= 0 then player.is_facing_right = player.impulse_x > 0 end if is_breaking and total_speed > breaking_speed then player.set_animation(49) elseif total_speed >= top_speed_x then player.set_animation(40) elseif total_speed > 0 then player.set_animation(1) -- Slower frame advance at low speed. Animation frames normally advance -- after scripts, so rewinding by one frame holds the frame longer. local frame_duration = 9 - (total_speed / 65) player.custom_value_1 = player.custom_value_1 + 1 if player.custom_value_1 >= frame_duration then player.custom_value_1 = 0 else player.current_animation_frame = player.current_animation_frame - 1 end else player.set_animation(0) end return false end Charge And Release Dash ¶ Hold one button to charge, tap another button to increase charge, release to dash. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local max_dash_speed = 786 if player.check_being_hit() then return false end -- Gradually bleed charge so repeated taps matter. player.custom_value_2 = player.custom_value_2 - player.custom_value_2 / 32 if player.pressed_button_c then player.custom_value_2 = player.custom_value_2 + 2 local pitch_percentage = 100 + player.custom_value_2 * 2 if pitch_percentage > 170 then pitch_percentage = 170 end player.play_sound("My Pack", "charge-tick", 2, pitch_percentage) player.jump_spam_timer = 0 player.special_spam_timer = 0 end if not player.is_holding_button_b then player.set_animation(48) local dash_speed = 8 + player.custom_value_2 / 2 dash_speed = (dash_speed * 255 * 255) / 1000 if dash_speed > max_dash_speed then dash_speed = max_dash_speed end player.impulse_x = dash_speed * player.direction_signal player.custom_value_2 = 0 player.jump_spam_timer = 0 player.special_spam_timer = 0 player.play_sound("My Pack", "dash-release", 2) end return false end
docs.title: Movement And Input

docs.text: These scripts cover player-owned movement: air steering, jump height, wall jumps, speed tiers, rolling momentum, and charge release. They are adapted from several Test chronicle prototypes and cleaned up into reusable patterns.
docs.title: Movement And Input Examples

docs.text: Attach this to a jump or aerial attack when you want the original controller to keep handling landing and collisions. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end -- Absolute left/right input is used for air steering because the player -- expects left to move left even if the character is facing right. local max_air_speed = 130 local acceleration = 7 if player.is_in_the_air then if player.is_holding_right and player.impulse_x < max_air_speed then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x + acceleration -- The previous-frame flag identifies the first held frame after a tap. -- Snap to the starting speed once, then clear the old input state so -- the snap is not applied again next frame. if player.was_previously_holding_right then player.impulse_x = max_air_speed player.previous_held_buttons = 0 end elseif player.is_holding_left and player.impulse_x > -max_air_speed then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x - acceleration if player.was_previously_holding_left then player.impulse_x = -max_air_speed player.previous_held_buttons = 0 end end end -- Only steering was changed. Let the jump controller keep running. return true end
docs.title: Simple Air Steering

docs.text: Use tiny setup scripts on different jump-start animations, then share one air-control script across all aerial states. Walk-jump setup: return function() local player = game.this_player if player ~= nil then -- Profile 1 means normal walk-jump steering. player.custom_value_1 = 1 end return true end Run-jump setup: return function() local player = game.this_player if player ~= nil then -- Profile 2 means faster run-jump steering. player.custom_value_1 = 2 end return true end Shared aerial script: return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local initial_velocity = 50 local max_velocity = 110 local acceleration = 16 if player.custom_value_1 == 2 then initial_velocity = 100 max_velocity = 190 acceleration = 20 end if player.is_in_the_air then if player.is_holding_right and player.impulse_x < max_velocity then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x + acceleration if player.was_previously_holding_right then player.impulse_x = initial_velocity player.previous_held_buttons = 0 end elseif player.is_holding_left and player.impulse_x > -max_velocity then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x - acceleration if player.was_previously_holding_left then player.impulse_x = -initial_velocity player.previous_held_buttons = 0 end end else -- Grounded direction changes update facing and reset to normal profile. if player.is_holding_right and not player.is_facing_right then player.is_facing_right = true player.custom_value_1 = 1 elseif player.is_holding_left and player.is_facing_right then player.is_facing_right = false player.custom_value_1 = 1 end end return true end

docs.text: This script shortens upward momentum when the player releases jump early. It can be layered into an existing jump script that still returns true . return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local small_jump_force = 262 -- Negative impulse_y means the character is rising. -- If the jump button is no longer held, clamp upward speed. if player.impulse_y < -small_jump_force and not player.is_holding_button_c then player.impulse_y = -small_jump_force end return true end
docs.title: Variable Jump Height

docs.text: Use this when an aerial attack owns movement and landing. It handles hits, gravity, horizontal steering, wall stopping, and landing. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local gravity = 14 local air_acceleration = 6 local top_speed = 393 -- Since this script replaces the controller, it must check interruptions. if player.check_being_hit() then return false end -- Let active hitboxes connect. If the move hits something, rebound both -- horizontal and vertical impulses to produce a bounce-like feel. if player.check_hitting_entities() then player.impulse_x = -player.impulse_x player.impulse_y = -player.impulse_y end player.impulse_y = player.impulse_y + gravity if player.is_holding_left then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x - air_acceleration elseif player.is_holding_right then player.impulse_x = player.impulse_x + air_acceleration end if player.impulse_x > top_speed then player.impulse_x = top_speed elseif player.impulse_x < -top_speed then player.impulse_x = -top_speed end player.velocity_x = player.impulse_x player.position_offset_y = player.position_offset_y + player.impulse_y if player.is_pressing_against_walls(true) then player.impulse_x = 0 end if player.impulse_y > 0 and player.position_offset_y >= 0 then player.impulse_y = 0 player.position_offset_y = 0 player.set_animation(0) player.object_mode = 2 end return false end
docs.title: Full Manual Air Physics

docs.text: This script freezes briefly on the wall, flips facing once, then lets the player launch away. return function() local player = game.this_player if player == nil then return true end local wall_freeze_frames = 8 if player.current_animation_frame < wall_freeze_frames then if player.current_animation_frame == 0 then -- Flip once at the start so forward now points away from the wall. player.is_facing_right = not player.is_facing_right end -- Stop the normal controller while the character clings to the wall. return false end local away_speed = 131 if player.is_holding_forward then away_speed = 196 elseif player.is_holding_backward then away_speed = 65 end player.velocity_x = away_speed * player.direction_signal player.impulse_y = player.impulse_y + 13 player.position_offset_y = player.position_offset_y + player.impulse_y if player.pressed_button_c and player.is_pressing_against_walls(true) then player.set_animation(56) player.impulse_y = -307 player.play_sound("My Pack", "wall-jump", 2) end return false end

docs.text: Projectiles And Item Examples ¶ Projectiles are standalone items. A projectile script usually runs with game.this_item , not game.this_character . If Lua owns the projectile's movement, return false so the fallback item controller does not move or destroy it a second time. Spawn A Projectile From A Character ¶ Attach this to the attack animation that should emit the projectile. return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end if character.current_animation_frame == 12 then character.try_spawn_item( "My Pack", -- pack containing the projectile entity "Fireball", -- projectile entity name 0, -- projectile animation id -1, -- object mode; -1 lets the spawned item keep defaults -2750, -- spawn X offset; helper applies source-facing rules -2750, -- spawn Y/depth offset -250, -- X velocity/impulse argument used by spawn helper 0, -- Y/depth velocity argument 90, -- lifetime in frames 8, -- projectile damage 4, -- hit pause when it connects "fireball-hit", -- optional hit sound "My Pack", -- hit sound pack 0 -- hit sound channel ) end -- Spawning is a one-time action. Let the attack controller continue. return true end Basic Projectile Physics ¶ Attach this to the projectile item's active animation. return function() local item = game.this_item if item == nil then return true end -- check_projectile_hits returns true when the projectile hit something. -- It also applies projectile damage/hit-pause/sound data configured at spawn. local should_destroy = item.check_projectile_hits() -- X is horizontal screen/world movement. item.velocity_x = item.velocity_x + item.impulse_x -- velocity_y is depth movement along the belt-scroller plane. item.velocity_y = item.velocity_y + item.impulse_z -- inner_timer is the usual projectile lifetime. item.inner_timer = item.inner_timer - 1 if item.inner_timer <= 0 then should_destroy = true end -- position_offset_y is height. Negative means above the ground. if item.position_offset_y < 0 or item.impulse_y < 0 then item.position_offset_y = item.position_offset_y + item.impulse_y if item.position_offset_y >= 0 then item.position_offset_y = 0 should_destroy = true end end -- Acceleration is applied after movement, matching the default item pattern. item.impulse_x = item.impulse_x + item.acceleration_x item.impulse_y = item.impulse_y + item.acceleration_y item.impulse_z = item.impulse_z + item.acceleration_z if item.update_position_and_check_world_collisions() then should_destroy = true item.play_sound("Classic", "SE10", 0) end if should_destroy then -- Switch to a hit/explosion animation and deactivate the projectile body. item.set_animation(48) item.is_active = false end return false end Projectile That Dies Without A Hit Animation ¶ Use this for effects that simply vanish when lifetime, landing, or wall collision ends them. return function() local item = game.this_item if item == nil then return true end local should_destroy = item.check_projectile_hits() item.velocity_x = item.velocity_x + item.impulse_x item.velocity_y = item.velocity_y + item.impulse_z item.inner_timer = item.inner_timer - 1 if item.inner_timer <= 0 then should_destroy = true end if item.position_offset_y < 0 or item.impulse_y < 0 then item.position_offset_y = item.position_offset_y + item.impulse_y if item.position_offset_y >= 0 then item.position_offset_y = 0 should_destroy = true end end item.impulse_x = item.impulse_x + item.acceleration_x item.impulse_y = item.impulse_y + item.acceleration_y item.impulse_z = item.impulse_z + item.acceleration_z if item.update_position_and_check_world_collisions() then should_destroy = true end if should_destroy then item.is_active = false item.object_mode = 0 end return false end Stationary Hitbox Or Freeze Field ¶ Use this for an item that should keep its current world position and ignore gravity. It still runs world collision so the object remains synchronized with the engine. return function() local item = game.this_item if item == nil then return true end -- This field is intentionally not moved by impulses. -- The entity can still have hitboxes in logic.json. item.impulse_x = 0 item.impulse_y = 0 item.impulse_z = 0 item.acceleration_x = 0 item.acceleration_y = 0 item.acceleration_z = 0 item.position_offset_y = 0 item.inner_timer = item.inner_timer - 1 if item.inner_timer <= 0 then item.is_active = false item.object_mode = 0 return false end item.update_position_and_check_world_collisions() return false end Projectile Burst ¶ Spawn many projectile angles from one animation frame. This is useful for fan shots, radial magic, or multi-shuriken bursts. -- Each row is animation id, velocity X, velocity Y/depth. Built once. local shots = { {0, 524, 0}, {1, 511, -116}, {2, 472, -227}, {3, 409, -326}, {4, 326, -409}, {5, 227, -472}, {6, 116, -511}, {7, 0, -524} } return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end if character.current_animation_frame == 20 then character.play_sound("My Pack", "burst", 2) for i = 1, #shots do local shot = shots[i] character.try_spawn_item( "My Pack", "Burst Projectile", shot[1], -1, -850, 2000, shot[2], shot[3], 60, 4, 2, "projectile-hit", "My Pack", 0 ) end end return true end Persistent Area Hitbox ¶ For a repeated-damage area, use an item for the visual/effect and a global or owner script for the repeated hit rule. This avoids relying on undocumented projectile fields. return function() local item = game.this_item if item == nil then return true end -- Keep the field alive for custom global logic. The global hook can scan -- active enemies and apply damage when their positions overlap this item. item.custom_value_1 = 1 item.inner_timer = item.inner_timer - 1 if item.inner_timer <= 0 then item.is_active = false item.object_mode = 0 end return false end Pair it with a pack-level post-update script: return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil or not character.is_enemy then return true end -- The actual area scan would loop over known area object IDs stored in -- custom values or use a known single spawned item ID. This compact example -- shows the damage-side rule only. if character.custom_value_8 > 0 then character.custom_value_8 = character.custom_value_8 - 1 return true end -- A real script should first check distance to the area item. -- Use custom_value_8 as a per-enemy cooldown so the same field can hit -- repeatedly without damaging every frame. character.damage_taken = 2 character.is_being_hit = true character.check_being_hit() character.custom_value_8 = 12 return true end Spawn An Enemy Helper ¶ The item layer also exposes try_spawn_enemy . Use it for minions, traps, or helper attacks. return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end if character.current_animation_frame == 30 then local helper_entity_id = 123456789 character.try_spawn_enemy( "My Pack", helper_entity_id, -- replace with the helper enemy's entity type/id 0, 0, -1000, 0 ) end return true end If your data uses entity names rather than numeric IDs, prefer SpawnEnemyEvent in logic events, which hashes entityName for you. The Lua helper is intentionally lower level and expects the entity type/id value.

Built once. local shots = { {0, 524, 0}, {1, 511, -116}, {2, 472, -227}, {3, 409, -326}, {4, 326, -409}, {5, 227, -472}, {6, 116, -511}, {7, 0, -524} } return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end if character.current_animation_frame == 20 then character.play_sound("My Pack", "burst", 2) for i = 1, #shots do local shot = shots[i] character.try_spawn_item( "My Pack", "Burst Projectile", shot[1], -1, -850, 2000, shot[2], shot[3], 60, 4, 2, "projectile-hit", "My Pack", 0 ) end end return true end
docs.title: Projectile Burst

docs.text: For a repeated-damage area, use an item for the visual/effect and a global or owner script for the repeated hit rule. This avoids relying on undocumented projectile fields. return function() local item = game.this_item if item == nil then return true end -- Keep the field alive for custom global logic. The global hook can scan -- active enemies and apply damage when their positions overlap this item. item.custom_value_1 = 1 item.inner_timer = item.inner_timer - 1 if item.inner_timer <= 0 then item.is_active = false item.object_mode = 0 end return false end Pair it with a pack-level post-update script: return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil or not character.is_enemy then return true end -- The actual area scan would loop over known area object IDs stored in -- custom values or use a known single spawned item ID. This compact example -- shows the damage-side rule only. if character.custom_value_8 > 0 then character.custom_value_8 = character.custom_value_8 - 1 return true end -- A real script should first check distance to the area item. -- Use custom_value_8 as a per-enemy cooldown so the same field can hit -- repeatedly without damaging every frame. character.damage_taken = 2 character.is_being_hit = true character.check_being_hit() character.custom_value_8 = 12 return true end
docs.title: Persistent Area Hitbox

docs.text: The item layer also exposes try_spawn_enemy . Use it for minions, traps, or helper attacks. return function() local character = game.this_character if character == nil then return true end if character.current_animation_frame == 30 then local helper_entity_id = 123456789 character.try_spawn_enemy( "My Pack", helper_entity_id, -- replace with the helper enemy's entity type/id 0, 0, -1000, 0 ) end return true end If your data uses entity names rather than numeric IDs, prefer SpawnEnemyEvent in logic events, which hashes entityName for you. The Lua helper is intentionally lower level and expects the entity type/id value.

docs.text: Modding With an AI Assistant ¶ The Windows version of the game ships with written instructions that let an AI assistant build mods for you: characters, enemies, items, reskins, levels, cutscenes, palettes, audio and Lua scripts. Any assistant that can read and write files in a folder on your computer will do. That means a coding agent you run on your machine or in an editor, not a plain chat window in a browser, which cannot reach the game folder. The instructions are plain text, so they work the same whichever one you use. What ships with the game ¶ Next to SOR2 New Era.exe : AGENTS.md the entry point: points the assistant at the instructions below .claude/skills/ sor2-new-era-modding/ shared rules, file-format reference, JSON schemas, mod validator sor2-mod-setup-and-sharing/ start a mod, game rules, difficulty, export and share sor2-create-character/ new playable characters, enemies and bosses sor2-reskin-classic/ new looks for Classic characters, stages and screens; palettes sor2-create-level/ levels, enemy waves, cutscenes, title and ending screens sor2-items-and-weapons/ pick-ups, weapons and breakable containers sor2-audio/ sounds, music and Classic audio replacement sor2-lua-scripting/ behaviour, AI, HUD and stage logic in Lua The folder is named .claude because some assistants look there on their own, but the files inside are ordinary Markdown that any assistant can read. The folder is hidden on some systems; keep it next to the executable either way. Using it ¶ Point the assistant at the game folder, the one containing SOR2 New Era.exe and Editor . Tell it to read AGENTS.md first. Some assistants find the instructions by themselves, but saying so costs nothing and makes sure it starts in the right place. Ask for what you want in your own words, for example "add a new enemy to my mod Street Justice that throws knives", and name the mod. Close the Character, Level and Audio editors before the assistant edits a mod: they rewrite whole files on save and would discard its changes. Test the result in game, then export it as usual. See Testing and Exporting . Results vary with the assistant you use, and it may get things wrong. Keep a backup of a mod you care about, and check its work in game. The assistant checks its work with the bundled validator, which needs Python. To run it yourself: python .claude/skills/sor2-new-era-modding/scripts/validate_mod.py "Editor/<Mod Name>" For the full schema checks, install jsonschema (and Pillow for palette checks) with pip install jsonschema Pillow . Mod editing, with or without an assistant, is only available on Windows.

docs.text: Asset Requirements ¶ Good assets make the editors easier to use and make exported mods more reliable. Goal ¶ Prepare images and audio before importing them into a mod. Images ¶ Use PNG for sprites, portraits, previews, thumbnails, palettes, and most level art. Prefer importing animated GIF for character and level animations. Use transparency for character sprites, effects, pickups, and foreground objects that should not have a rectangular background. Keep sprite scale consistent across a character. If one frame is drawn at a different scale, hitboxes and pivots become harder to tune. Keep filenames simple. Short names using letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, and underscores are easiest to manage. Avoid resizing frames after you have tuned pivots, hitboxes, body boxes, or throw offsets. For level art, prefer building a level from small reusable parts. Reuse background elements as possible. Consider building layers as tilemaps, using the grid feature in the editor. This makes levels faster to load when compared to using one single giant image for the entire scene. Character frames ¶ The Character Editor can import loose PNG files and animated GIF files. After import, check: Pivot position on every frame. Body box during idle, walking, jumping, attacking, being hit, and falling. Hitboxes only on active attack frames. Grab and throw offsets. Weapon points or projectile spawn points when an animation uses them. Characters with color palettes are converted to a maximum of 255 colors. If a character doesn't have at least one color palette (a default palette), then once exported, the community can't create new color palettes for it. Palettes ¶ Use palette images created by the editor whenever possible. It is, however, possible to create them manually using any image editing program. They are maximum 255 pixels width by 1 pixel height, one pixel per color. Keep palette files in the correct target folder: entity-owned palettes under the entity folder, external palettes under Palettes/<Target Mod>/<Target Entity> . Test every palette in-game using editor test mode, then verify the exported mod. A palette can look fine in isolation but clash with shadows, hit flashes, or HUD icons. Audio ¶ The Audio Editor accepts WAV , MP3 , and OGG . Use short files for hit sounds, voices, and menu sounds, typically as WAV . Use music-length files for stage music and cutscene music, preferably OGG or MP3 . Set loop points for tracks that should loop cleanly. Keep replacement audio names clear enough to identify the target sound or music. Test volume in-game, not only in the editor preview. Keep sounds and music files small, as they impact level loading times. Scripts ¶ Lua scripts are plain .lua files under Scripts . Avoid renaming scripts once animation logic references them. Prefer one clear behavior per script. Test scripts with two or more players online, enemies on screen, and edge cases such as grabs, death, knockdown, and scene transitions. Don't export and share mods with scripts until they are well tested. A faulty script may stale the game. Related pages ¶ Mod Folder Anatomy Playable Character From Scratch Add Custom Audio Lua API Reference

docs.text: Installing Community Mods ¶ Mods are usually shared as exported .cne files. You might find them through community links, such as links shared on the Streets of Rage 2 New Era Discord. Goal ¶ Install a shared mod into your game and know what to do if the author sends editable source files instead. Where the Mods folder is ¶ Platform Mods folder Windows Mods , next to the game's executable Linux Mods , next to the game's executable. If that folder can't be created, ~/.config/unity3d/gsaurus/SOR2 New Era/Mods macOS ~/Library/Application Support/gsaurus/SOR2 New Era/Mods Android Private to the game. Use Extras -> Add Mods (see below) On macOS and Linux, Extras -> Add Mods can also switch to a different Mods folder: select a folder instead of mod files. If you received an exported mod ¶ On Windows, macOS and Linux: Download the mod file. It is usually a .cne file. Close the game if it is already running. Move the .cne mod file into the game's Mods folder. Run Streets of Rage 2 New Era. The game scans Mods automatically and adds the mod to the available mod list. Select either Local Game or Online Game , then select the mod from the list to play. On Android, or to skip finding the folder on macOS and Linux: Download the mod file ( .cne or .zip ). In the game, open Extras -> Add Mods . Browse to the downloaded file and select it. You can select several at once. The game copies the mod into its Mods folder and loads it right away. Adding a mod with the same name replaces the previous version. On Android 10 and newer, the file browser first asks for a folder through the system picker: choose the folder you downloaded the mod to, such as Download . If the mod does not appear ¶ Confirm the file is in Mods , not Editor . On macOS and Linux, check the table above: the folder is not always next to the game. Confirm the file has the .cne extension. Restart the game if you didn't after adding the mod in the Mods folder. If the game reports missing or mismatching dependencies, download the required dependency mods and also add them to the Mods folder. Make sure you got the correct versions. If you received source files ¶ Source mods are simply folders with content inside. Opening and editing them needs the in-game editor, which is only available on Windows. On other platforms, ask the author for the exported .cne file. Place the whole source folder in Editor (unzip it first if you downloaded it as a .zip file). Run Streets of Rage 2 New Era. Open the in-game editor menu ( Extras -> Editor ). Open the mod from the editor list. Test or export it from the editor. The source folder should normally contain config.json and may contain folders such as Entities , Levels , Sounds , Musics , Palettes , or Scripts . Multiplayer ¶ Both players need the same mod version. New Era compares mod checksums; the mod name alone is not enough. If multiplayer reports a missing mod or mismatching checksums, the players must exchange the same version of the mod and then restart the game. Related pages ¶ Testing and Exporting Package, Export, and Share

docs.text: Launch Tools ¶ The modding tools come with the game installation. Open the right editor for the content you want to add or change. Open the in-game editor menu ¶ Run Streets of Rage 2 New Era. From the main menu, select Extras -> Editor . Create a new mod or open an existing mod. Choose the tool you need for the current task. The in-game editor menu lets you edit mod metadata, such as description and thumbnail, general game mechanics, difficulty levels, and dependencies to other mods. It is also the main entry point for testing your mod, and exporting it, so it becomes available locally in the main game, and can then be shared with the community. Pick the right tool ¶ Settings : name, description, thumbnail, dependencies, general game settings. Characters : create or edit playable characters, enemies and items, or reskin the ones from the Classic game. Color Palettes : color sets for your own entities, entities from the Classic game, or for entities from other community mods. Levels : create or edit game levels and cutscenes, or reskin the ones from the Classic game, or reskin the title screen of the main menu itself. Audio : setup sounds and music to use in your mod, or as replacements for the ones used in the Classic game. Scripts : opens the Scripts folder of your mod. Use any IDE with support for Lua, or any text editor of your choice, to create and edit behavior for your characters, or for the community to reuse. Each standalone editor has a page describing its interface — the panels, the mouse controls in its preview, and its keyboard shortcuts. Read the one for the tool you are about to use: The Character Editor Workspace The Level Editor Workspace The Audio Editor Workspace Opening a source mod ¶ Editable mods are folders under Editor . If someone sends you source files instead of an exported .cne file, place the whole folder in Editor , run the game, open the in-game editor menu, and choose that mod from the editor list. Playing an exported mod ¶ Playable mods are .cne files under Mods . If someone sends you an exported mod, place the .cne file into Mods . Run the game, and let the game auto-detect it. Related pages ¶ Installing Community Mods Mod Folder Anatomy Create a Custom Mod Package, Export, and Share

docs.text: Mod Folder Anatomy ¶ A New Era mod has two forms: an editable source folder, or an exported playable mod. Goal ¶ Understand where files belong so the game and editors can find them. Source mod folder ¶ Source mods live in Editor : Editor/ My Mod/ config.json thumbnail.png Entities/ Entity Replacements/ Levels/ Art/ Level Replacements/ Classic/ Palettes/ Sounds/ Musics/ Audio Replacements/ Music Replacements/ Scripts/ Only the folders your mod uses need to exist. The editors create and manage these folders as needed. Common files and folders ¶ config.json : mod settings, dependencies, gameplay options, character availability, and other pack-level data. thumbnail.png : image shown in mod lists. Entities : playable characters, enemies, items, and containers owned by this mod. Entity Replacements : replacements for entities from another pack, commonly Classic . Level Replacements : replacement level art and presentation data for another pack, commonly Classic . Levels : level data, cutscene data, presentation screens, ending data, and level art references. Levels/Art : background, foreground, and cutscene images used by level data. Palettes : palettes that target entities from another pack, such as Classic characters. Entities/<Entity Name>/Palettes : palettes for an entity owned by this mod. Sounds : sounds and voices owned by this mod. Musics : music tracks owned by this mod. Audio Replacements : mappings that replace sounds, voices, or music from another pack. Scripts : Lua files referenced by animation logic or pack-level update hooks. Entity folders ¶ An entity folder usually contains: Entities/ My Fighter/ 0.png 1.png animations.json logic.json spriteSettings.json dependencies.json preview.png portrait.png Palettes/ palette 0.png The Character Editor manages the JSON files. You normally edit sprites and animation data through the editor alone. Hand-editing is possible, for particular cases. Level files ¶ Levels commonly use paired files: level 1.json : gameplay layout, waves, spawns, walls, and scroll limits. level 1 - art.json : visual scene data and background layers. level 1 - cutscenes.json : optional cutscene data for that level. presentation.json , ending.json , and similar files: non-gameplay presentation sequences. Use the Level Editor for these files. It keeps the level data, visual data, and referenced art aligned. Exported mod package ¶ Exported mods live in Mods : Mods/ My Mod.cne The exported .cne is what players copy, upload, and share. The game auto-detects the mods present in Mods folder when it starts. Related pages ¶ Pack Layout and Conventions for the exact naming and resolution rules. Asset Requirements Testing and Exporting Package, Export, and Share

docs.text: Testing and Exporting ¶ Testing catches mod problems while they are still small. Exporting turns your editable source folder into a playable .cne mod. Goal ¶ Test a mod in-game, export it, and understand what the exported file is for. Test in the editor ¶ Open the mod from the game editor menu ( Extras -> Editor ) and choose Test . The mod is played as it is, without exporting first. A mod rarely is a whole game, so anything it doesn't provide itself is borrowed from 30th Anniversary for the duration of the test: levels, characters, gameplay settings, HUD, palettes and cutscenes. If that pack is unavailable, Test falls back to Classic. A mod with only a character is played through the reference levels; a mod with only a level is played with the reference characters; a mod with only gameplay settings uses your settings. Reskins are tested too: a presentation-only skin runs 30th Anniversary with your mod as the active skin, so replaced character art, level art, cutscenes, sounds and music all show up. The base pack supplies gameplay and the roster. Your own skin preferences in the options menu are left untouched, and the previous session settings are restored when you leave Test. Test is greyed out only when there is nothing the game could show - a mod with just color palettes, for instance. Any playable character, level, cutscene or reskin enables it, and so does marking the mod as playable in the export settings. Check: The mod appears with the correct name and thumbnail. Playable characters appear in the character select screen. Enemies spawn with the expected palette, health, behavior, and sounds. Bodyboxes and hitboxes seen in test mode are coherent. Level walls, scroll limits, enemy waves, and item drops work. Cutscenes end and transition correctly. Music loops cleanly and sounds play at the right volume. Lua scripts do not break when the move misses, hits multiple targets, and framerate remains smooth. Export the mod ¶ From the mod editor menu: Choose Export . Wait for the export to complete. Find the exported .cne in Mods . The exported mod is what you upload, send to friends, or post to a community link. Other players place that exported file in their own Mods folder and the game auto-detects it. Test after export ¶ Test that the exported mod behaves as expected: Test color palettes. Test online multiplayer, specially if your mod uses Lua scripts. Confirm framerate keeps stable. Confirm music loops smoothly. Check level loading times. Loading times may take longer in exported mods than during editor testing - this happens due to compression and optimizations for runtime performance. Multiplayer checks ¶ All players must have the same mod version. The game checks checksum equality for the loaded mod and dependencies. If a player has a different version, or a dependency with a different checksum, multiplayer may reject the session and report the mismatching versions.
