docs.title: Goal

docs.text: Open the mod from the game editor menu ( Extras -> Editor ) and choose Test . The mod is played as it is, without exporting first. A mod rarely is a whole game, so anything it doesn't provide itself is borrowed from 30th Anniversary for the duration of the test: levels, characters, gameplay settings, HUD, palettes and cutscenes. If that pack is unavailable, Test falls back to Classic. A mod with only a character is played through the reference levels; a mod with only a level is played with the reference characters; a mod with only gameplay settings uses your settings. Reskins are tested too: a presentation-only skin runs 30th Anniversary with your mod as the active skin, so replaced character art, level art, cutscenes, sounds and music all show up. The base pack supplies gameplay and the roster. Your own skin preferences in the options menu are left untouched, and the previous session settings are restored when you leave Test. Test is greyed out only when there is nothing the game could show - a mod with just color palettes, for instance. Any playable character, level, cutscene or reskin enables it, and so does marking the mod as playable in the export settings. Check: The mod appears with the correct name and thumbnail. Playable characters appear in the character select screen. Enemies spawn with the expected palette, health, behavior, and sounds. Bodyboxes and hitboxes seen in test mode are coherent. Level walls, scroll limits, enemy waves, and item drops work. Cutscenes end and transition correctly. Music loops cleanly and sounds play at the right volume. Lua scripts do not break when the move misses, hits multiple targets, and framerate remains smooth.

docs.text: What You Can Build ¶ What New Era mods can do: Custom Mod, which may be: - A new playable game mod, or - A non-playable mod, destined to provide tools and components for use in other mods. E.g. Lua scripts, enemies pack, etc. Reskinning, including: - New color palettes for characters in the original game or for other community mods. - Reskin the classic Streets of Rage 2 game - applied to any mod using the classic content, such as 30th Anniversary and Ninpo Kage Bunshin . A reskin can also replace the title screen art and music. The same mod can provide a combination of those. For example, it can add a new playable character, replace classic music, add a new color palette for Blaze and provide a new title screen. Custom Mod ¶ Creating a new game, or content for use in new playable mods. Playable characters : custom sprites, animations, physics, hitboxes, throws information, icon, character select portrait, and optional Lua behavior. Enemies : custom sprites, animations, physics, swap of their classic behaviors, and optional Lua behavior. Items : breakable containers, and any objects spawned on levels, or by players or enemies, such as projectiles. Levels : layered background and foreground art organized in parallax layers, animated art, enemy spawns, item placement, camera limits, walls, music, transitions, and level effects. Cutscenes and endings : non-playable scene sequences built with level-style layers, and automatic transition timings. Color palettes : alternate colors for playable characters and entities from your mod. Audio : custom sounds, voices, music, and their loop points. Lua scripts : animation logic, projectiles, AI decisions, movement rules, reactions, and other runtime behavior. Reskinning ¶ Changing how the original Streets of Rage 2 game looks or sounds, while keeping its original gameplay intact. Classic playable characters : replace their sprites, icons, portraits, and add additional color palettes. Classic enemies and items : replace their sprites and color palettes, weapons, pickups, containers, projectiles. Classic level art : redesign level layers art and respective parallax settings. Classic cutscenes : The original game doesn't have cutscenes, but you can add your own. Classic ending : replace the original ending screens. Character select screen : art and parallax settings. Classic music : replacement tracks and loop points. Classic sounds : replacement voices and sound effects. Main title screen : art and parallax settings for the background presentation in the main menu. Classic reskins do not change logic. For example, a reskin can make Galsia look and sound different, but Galsia still behaves the same. Start here when the project is mainly visual or audio replacement for the classic game. Picking a First Task ¶ Pick the smallest task that matches the mod you actually want to make. For a custom mod: Create a Custom Mod Create a Playable Character From Scratch Create Custom Levels For a classic reskin: Reskin Workflow Add New Color Palettes Replace Classic Music Reskin the Title Screen Reskin Classic Characters Reskin Classic Levels For sharing or testing: Testing and Exporting Package, Export, and Share Installing Community Mods
